129	
130	**Instances by reference (ADR-LAY-01).** A template is authored, immutable and lives in the frozen `SectionTemplates` catalog; an instance is a row in `layout.state` that names a template by its `template_id` string and carries only what can differ between two instances of one template: its ids, body, offset, id bases, drift hashes and socket/weld history. Full geometry in the block would multiply rectangles by sections, duplicate authored data, defeat the Vertical Slice "seed plus deltas" model and let an exporter bug corrupt the world permanently; a second `layout.templates` block would add a second restore root for nothing. Both are rejected (§ Alternatives 1 and 2).
131	
132	**Two objects, one owner.** The module owns two plain `RefCounted` objects:
133	
134	- **`LayoutState`** holds the persisted tables of § 2 as typed fields. It is the object the block descriptor's callables read and write; `restore` copies into it and never replaces it (ADR-0003 § 2), because the read-view facade `LayoutViews` wraps it for the life of the process.
135	- **`LayoutDerived`** holds everything that is rebuilt from `LayoutState`, the templates and the Graph and is **never snapshotted or hashed**: the `section_id`-indexed lookup columns, the socket-ref index, the live-count caps, the leaf cache and `opening_leaves` map (§ 8), the three version counters and `changed_region` stamps (§ 7), `mutation_count`, and the handle to ADR-0014's broadphase. The split is what makes "derived caches are never persisted" (TR-section-004) checkable: a test snapshots `LayoutState` only, and the allow-list test of AC-130 walks only that payload.
136	
137	**What the block never holds.** Floats; geometry; the section `kind` (the Graph's section record owns it, LS-17); a `visited` bit (the block is WORLD-scoped and rolls back on `request_restore`); a loose-item table (Interaction's `interaction.state` holds it and lists `layout.state` in its own `restore_after`); a door `area` or `door_state`; atmosphere; pose, velocity or any `body.state` field; a stored `layout_hash` or `mutation_count` (Save/Load's `block_state_hash` owns the stored copy, LY D.10, OQ-36). This is TR-section-028 and the first half of TR-section-013.
138	
139	**Source layout (ADR-0010).** `src/sim/layout/`: `layout_module.gd` (owner, registration, callables), `layout_state.gd`, `layout_derived.gd`, `layout_ids.gd`, `socket_ref.gd`, `layout_faults.gd`, `layout_mutators.gd` (LM1 to LM4 and checks), `weld_math.gd` and `detach_planner.gd` (pure), `door_leaves.gd` (the hook), `layout_restore.gd` (validation), `views/` (`LayoutViews` and the record classes of § 11), `ports/layout_graph_port.gd` (`@abstract`, § 8). The PROJECTOR is `src/presentation/projector/` and is never imported from here. The pure compile of authored runs into the rect table (`TemplateCompiler`) lives under `src/data/sections/` beside the loader that calls it, owned by Layout by review, not by import (ADR-0007 § 1.9).
140	
141	### 2. The snapshot payload: dense parallel columns, ascending ids, tombstones kept
142	
143	`snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload)` with a `Dictionary` whose keys are `String`s. Every table is a set of **parallel columns** (TR-section-006): no `Dictionary` is keyed by an id, no `Vector2i`/`Rect2i`/`Color`/`Resource`/`StringName`, no `PackedStringArray`, and every packed array in the payload is a `duplicate()` (ADR-0003 snapshot contract; registry `live_reference_in_snapshot_payload`). The key set is closed; the AC-130 allow-list file is regenerated from this table.
144	
145	| Payload key | Type | Contents (row order) |
146	|---|---|---|
147	| `schema_version` | `int` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` |
148	| `counters` | `Dictionary` of three `int`s | `next_section_id`, `next_body_id`, `next_room_id` (first allocated id is 1, so `default_state` sets all three to 1) |
149	| `bodies` | `Dictionary` | `body_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `origin_section_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `state` (`PackedByteArray`: 0 `LIVE`, 1 `DISSOLVED`); ascending `body_id` |
150	| `instances` | `Dictionary` of 14 columns | `section_id`, `body_id`, `offset_x`, `offset_y`, `room_id_base`, `node_base`, `edge_base`, `comp_base`, `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash`, `structure_hash` (all `PackedInt32Array`); `rot_q`, `discarded` (`PackedByteArray`); `template_id` (`Array[String]`); ascending `section_id` |
151	| `sockets` | `Dictionary` | `section_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `socket_index` (`PackedByteArray`), `state` (`PackedByteArray`: 1 `WELDED`, 2 `CAPPED`, 3 `CUT_OPEN`; `FREE` = 0 is never stored), `seam_id` (`PackedInt32Array`); ascending `(section_id, socket_index)`; only non-`FREE` sockets have a row |
152	| `welds` | `Dictionary` | `seam_id`, `section_a`, `section_b` (`PackedInt32Array`), `socket_a`, `socket_b`, `state` (`PackedByteArray`; `state`: 0 `ACTIVE`, 1 `CUT_SEALED`, 2 `CUT_RAGGED`), `welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T` (`PackedInt64Array`); ascending `seam_id` |
153	
154	Decisions inside the shape:
155	
156	- **Ids are dense ordinals: `section_id == row + 1` and `body_id == row + 1`.** A section or body id is consumed only by the mutator that appends its row, in the same call, so no id exists without a row. Row lookup is then an index, not a map: no `Dictionary` on the read path, no `bsearch` for the common query. Restore verifies the equality (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`). The cost is that a future "reserve an id then maybe not use it" idea is forbidden by this ADR, which is the right pressure (§ Risks R1).
157	- **`template_id` is a typed `Array[String]` column** (TR-section-004). The alternatives were the ledger integer (rejected: the GDD allow-list, LY-6 b and every restore reason name the string; four templates; saves are disposable pre-release; a human-readable dump matters more than 4 bytes a row) and a `PackedStringArray` (rejected: not on ADR-0006's allow-list). **Probed 2026-10-29:** a typed `Array[String]` survives `var_to_bytes`/`bytes_to_var` still typed.
158	- **64-bit times are native `PackedInt64Array` columns** (TR-section-006). ADR-0006 § 1.2 item 3 allows full-width `int` and § 1.3 limits the halves convention to values that can reach JSON; `welded_at_T`/`cut_at_T` reach JSON only through the dev `dump-save`, which renders any `int` of magnitude 2^53 or more as a decimal string and `T` is bounded below 2^53. The GDD's two-halves form stays legal and is not used.
159	- **The three hashes are stored as signed int32 and compared as `value & 0xFFFFFFFF`** (`IntMath.low32`, ADR-0005 P9; probed 2026-10-29). A comparison without the mask is a lint-visible defect (AC-172 c).
160	- **`rot_q` is a byte column that must be 0.** It is stored so the field exists in schema v1 and a later rotation feature is not a layout change; any nonzero value is `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED` at restore and a boot error in a template that asks for it.
161	- **`socket_index` is the template's declaration ordinal** of that socket, a `uint8` (MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION never exceeds 8 and is lint-bounded by `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION`). A runtime socket handle is the packed int `SocketRef = (section_id << 4) | socket_index` (`socket_ref.gd`, 24 bits at the section-id ceiling), used as an argument, a memo key and a sort key; it is never persisted.
162	- **Seam ids are the Graph's.** A `welds` row's `seam_id` is whatever `weld_join` returned; Layout allocates none and treats it as an opaque positive `int32`. After a cut the two sockets keep their `seam_id` (state `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN`) because the scar's bead and cap plate are drawn from that history (Pillar 5).
163	- **The payload size rule holds.** The largest realistic shape (D.21's long campaign) is tens of KB, far under `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`; `snapshot()` computes the D.21 estimate from row counts and raises the one-shot diagnostic `layout_block_soft_bytes` when it exceeds `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` (GDD Tuning Knobs); the hard ceiling is Save/Load's (TR-section-030).
164	
165	**Tombstones.** A discarded section keeps its row with `discarded = 1` and its `body_id`; the body it sat on becomes `DISSOLVED`; its `socket` and `welds` rows stay (a surviving mate keeps its `CAPPED`/`CUT_OPEN` history). Ids stay consumed, so nothing is ever reused or renumbered (TR-section-005).
166	
167	### 3. ID allocation and the split with the Graph (ADR-LAY-05)
168	
169	| Id | Allocator | Counter and home | Range and rule |
170	|---|---|---|---|
171	| `section_id` | **Layout** | `next_section_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^20 - 1` so `rect_key` fits 32 bits (D.9); `can_build` returns `CAPACITY` before consuming `2^20` |
172	| `body_id` | **Layout** | `next_body_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^31 - 1` (int32 column); one new id per LM1 and per LM3 |
173	| `room_id` | **Layout** | `next_room_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^31 - 1`; **contiguous per instance**: `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`, `room_index` the room's declaration order in the template |
174	| `node_id`, `edge_id`, `compartment_id` | **Graph** | `next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, comp counter in `graph.state` | returned by M1 as `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` and stored by Layout per instance as `graph_ref_base` |
175	| `seam_id`, opening ids | **Graph** | `next_seam_id` in `graph.state` | given to Layout in LM2's arguments and read back through `seam_view` |
176	| `section_id` in `graph.state` | follows Layout | `next_section_id` in `graph.state` | M1 advances it to `max(section_id) + 1`; Layout never reads it except in the post-restore verification |
177	
178	**Mapping rules (all derived, none persisted).**
179	
180	- Template-local index to Graph id: `node_id = node_base + node_ref_index`, `edge_id = edge_base + edge_ref_index`; template-local room to compartment: `comp_id = comp_base + room_index`; room to id: `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`. Hence `compartment_of_room(room_id) = comp_base(section) + (room_id - room_id_base(section))` and the inverse.
181	- Reverse lookup (a Graph id or a `room_id` to its section) is a `bsearch` over the ascending base column (`node_base`, `edge_base`, `comp_base`, `room_id_base` are all ascending because every allocator is monotone and rows append). A section whose range does not contain the id answers `NONE` (a discarded section's `anchor_geometry` answers nothing, without an error, FT:703).
182	- These rules require the Graph to return **contiguous** node, edge and compartment ranges **in template order** from M1 (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011) and to size each range from the template alone, so the post-restore check "node, edge and compartment counts match the template" is a pure comparison.
183	
184	**When ids are consumed.** LM1 reads (does not yet advance) `next_section_id`, `next_body_id` and `next_room_id`, calls the Graph's M1 with the section id, and only on an `OK` status appends the rows and advances the counters. So a Graph defect leaves Layout's counters and tables untouched (fail-closed per ADR-0003 § 5; the kernel is `FAULTED` anyway). `can_build` and `can_detach` test every counter ceiling **before** any id is consumed or the Graph is called, so no counter ever wraps (TR-section-037).
185	
186	**Why Layout owns the section id.** The Graph's M1 takes "a caller section id" (LS-15, LS-19), the Graph's `next_section_id` then follows Layout's, and Layout needs the section id to exist before the Graph does (it keys the dirty key and the body row). The alternative of the Graph allocating it (§ Alternatives 4) would make Layout's `build_section` depend on a return value to name its own row and would put the `rect_key` bound (2^20) in the Graph's hands.
187	
188	### 4. Template identity, the ledger nesting (OQ-B) and the three hashes (ADR-LAY-04, -06)
189	
190	**Ledger nesting (ADR-0007 OQ-B).** `assets/data/sections/ids.lock.json` is one `section_templates` space with one flat `pairs[]`, exactly the shape ADR-0007 § 3.2 defines, so `LedgerCheck.verify` stays generic and the append-only CI gate needs no second format. Two classes share the space, told apart by **key shape**: a template pair has key `<template_id>`, a room pair has key `<template_id>/<room_key>` (the `/` is illegal inside a snake_case key, so the split is unambiguous). Template ids come from the low part of the declared range and room ids from above a fixed boundary (a `SectionLedgerCheck` in `src/data/sections/`, owned by Layout by review, checks the boundary, that every room pair's prefix is a template pair in the same ledger, and that retiring or dormanting a template does the same to its room pairs: lint `LEDGER_ROOM_ORPHAN`). One entry per `room_key` rather than a nested list keeps `dormant` and `retired_ids` per room, so removing one room from a template is a per-pair `dormant` flip and a renamed room is a visible new pair, which is the diff a migration step needs. The integers are **not persisted in `layout.state`** (the instance persists the `template_id` string, § 2); they exist so a rename or removal after `SHIPPED` is detected and migrated (ADR-0007 § 3.3), and so later blocks can reference a room by integer if they must.
191	
192	**The three hashes (the shape of ADR-LAY-06).** ADR-0005 § 3.1 forbids an owner-written `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` byte string, and § 4.6 already defines the template hashes as `Hash64.of_value` of a post-cast sub-payload "whose shape is Layout's and ADR-0013's". So ADR-LAY-06 becomes the **`Dictionary` shape of three sub-payloads**, hashed once by `SectionTemplates` at catalog freeze and stored as `low32` in the template row (never in the template file, ADR-0007 § 3.5):
193	
194	| Hash | Payload (keys sorted by the encoder, so order in source is irrelevant; every family is one flat `PackedInt32Array` in the field order of its LY-4 row, strings replaced by template-local indices, variable-length members as a CSR `*_off` array plus a data array) | Changes when |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `geometry_hash` | `size_tiles`; `rooms` (origin, flags, tile runs); `wall_runs` (orientation, start, length, kind, flanking rooms, `face_h_px`, `face_variant`); the compiled `rects` (stride 7: `x0, y0, x1, y1, flags, owner_kind, owner_ref`, in `idx` order, leaf and variant slots at their closed or full extent); `doors`; `sockets` with their `lanes`; `hardpoints`; `plate_positions`; `loose_slots`; `story_slots`; `anchors` (polyline CSR); `fixture_anchors`; `instrument_placements` (geometry fields only) | anything that decides where a rectangle, tile, socket, door or anchor is |
197	| `visual_hash` | `dialect`; kit-piece ids and layers; art references; labels; advisory hints (`socket_tag`); flags no query reads | only presentation changes |
198	| `structure_hash` | the **ordered** key sequences: `room_key[]`, `socket_key[]`, `door_key[]`, `hp_key[]`, `node_ref[]`, `edge_ref[]`, `anchor_key[]`, `slot_id[]`; each room's sorted tile list | any reorder, add, remove or rename of an identity-bearing element, or any tile-set change |
199	
200	**Why a third hash.** LY-26 e classifies a template change as "structural" when the *sets* of keys or a room's tile set differ, but the block persists only two hashes, so the check has nothing to compare against except Graph counts. A pure **reordering** (rooms `[a, b]` to `[b, a]`) keeps every set equal and every count equal, yet `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`, `socket_index` and `comp_base + room_index` all index the *current* template by position, so an existing save would silently attach its Graph compartments and welded sockets to the wrong rooms and sockets. LY-6 e's sentence "a template that merely reorders rooms changes ids only for NEW instances" is therefore wrong as written. The remedy is to persist what the check needs: `structure_hash` is one more `int32` per instance (§ 2), costs four bytes a row, and makes the structural rule exact: **a `structure_hash` mismatch is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` for every instance, history or not**, because every instance has Graph data built from the old order. `geometry_hash` keeps the GDD's history-dependent rule (§ 10). The third hash is not redundant with `geometry_hash`: because `rooms` are encoded in declaration order, a reorder already changes `geometry_hash`, which on an instance **with history** is refused by the GDD's own rule; the marginal value of `structure_hash` is the **never-welded `FREE` instance**, where the history-dependent rule would accept the change as `geometry_changed_fresh` and silently re-point `room_id_base + room_index`, `comp_base + room_index` and `socket_index` to the wrong rooms and sockets. This is a deliberate deviation from the TR text "13-int section-instance rows" (the row is 14 columns, one of them the string); it is listed first among the decisions for the user's review.
201	
202	**Two more template rules.** (a) Every coordinate of a footprint rectangle, socket `line_px`/`start_px`, room `origin_px` and wall run lies on the 24-px grid (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`) except a door leaf's moving edge (LY-3 a, LY-7); `GRID_24` is a **BOOT invariant** (`CONTENT_INVARIANT`, ADR-0007 § 2.4), not only a CI lint, because the closure of the weld offset on the grid (§ 7) and the broadphase cell alignment depend on it; a 12-px shift in a socket fails the load (TR-derelict-033 Layout half). (b) `area_max <= 0` on a door is the one named structural invariant D.5 needs (it divides by it) and refuses the load; the published `area_max` range is guidance (ADR-0007 § 2.5).
203	
204	### 5. Rectangles, units and frames: the record, the flags and the reserved `idx` space
205	
206	ADR-0014 owns the broadphase, `QueryBuffer`, `OccluderSource` and the query signatures. This ADR owns **what a rectangle is, how it is keyed and which ones can exist**.
207	
208	- **The record (TR-section-010).** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, **half-open** `[x0, x1) x [y0, y1)` over pixel cells, with one flags byte: `SOLID`, `OCCLUDES_LIGHT`, `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL` (registry `layout_rect_flags`). The legal flag combinations are LY-7's table and a boot error otherwise (`RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`). A rect with `x1 <= x0` or `y1 <= y0` is omitted from every result but keeps its `idx`.
209	- **Units and frames.** The unit is the base pixel; `TILE_PX` is the floor tile and `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` the wall depth. There is no world frame in Layout. Reads answer **section-local** except those that answer for one body (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `section_at`, `weld_offset`, `detach_preview`), which answer in the **body frame** = section-local + `offset_px(section_id)` (LY-3 c).
210	- **Transforms are integer translation only.** No rotation, no mirror, no zoom value appears anywhere in Layout (LY-3 d, e). Every px-to-tile or px-to-cell conversion is **floor** division through `IntMath.floor_div` (body-frame coordinates may be negative after a detach re-base); the bare `/` and `%` operators appear nowhere in `src/sim/layout/` (ADR-0010 `SIM-05`).
211	- **The `idx` space is compiled once per template and never changes** (D.9): static rects sorted by `(y0, x0, y1, x1, flags)` are `0 .. N_static - 1`; one reserved leaf slot per door follows in door declaration order; two reserved variant slots (PLATE, JAMB) per **hatched** socket follow, `idx = N_static + N_doors + 2h + v`. The key `(section_id, idx)` is therefore stable across attach, detach, restore and animation: a state change only switches slots between active and inactive; an inactive or zero-length slot is omitted from results and keeps its `idx` (TR-section-020's "renumbers nothing" half).
212	- **Rect keys.** `rect_key = section_id * RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` with the stride `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` (GDD Tuning Knobs, a power of two) and `idx < stride`; the key reaches `2^32 - 1`, so every key column is `PackedInt64Array` (ADR-0014 owns the buffer). Boot refuses a template whose `N_static + N_doors + 2 N_hatched` exceeds the stride (`RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW`).
213	- **The compiled table is catalog data.** `SectionTemplate` exposes rect `idx`-indexed accessors (`rect_count()`, `rect_x0(i)`, `rect_y0(i)`, `rect_x1(i)`, `rect_y1(i)`, `rect_flags(i)`, `rect_owner_kind(i)`, `rect_owner_ref(i)`), never a packed array (ADR-0007 § 1.5). The bulk read that builds a body's grid at build, attach, detach and restore is ADR-0014's; those events are cold, so accessor calls are acceptable there (V3 measures them).
214	- **Static footprint set versus query set.** `rects_in` returns `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rects and `solid_in` returns `SOLID` rects in their *current leaf state*; the mating overlap test of § 6 uses the **static** set with all flags, so a door animating can never flip a verdict. Both sets are views of one rect set (Pillar 1: collision, light and drawing cannot disagree); neither is an engine collision shape, and the avatar has no physics body.
215

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header

engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

# TD-ADR — Architecture Decision Review

Agent: `technical-director` | Model tier: Opus | Domain: Architecture, engine risk, performance

**Trigger**: After an individual ADR is authored (`/architecture-decision`), before
it is marked Accepted

**Context to pass**:
- ADR file path
- Engine version and knowledge gap risk level for the domain
- Related ADRs (if any)

**Prompt**:
> "Review this Architecture Decision Record. Does it have a clear problem statement
> and rationale? Are the rejected alternatives genuinely considered? Does the
> Consequences section acknowledge the trade-offs honestly? Is the engine version
> stamped? Are post-cutoff API risks flagged? Does it link to the GDD requirements
> it covers? Return APPROVE, CONCERNS [specific gaps], or REJECT [the decision is
> underspecified or makes unsound technical assumptions]."

**Verdicts**: APPROVE / CONCERNS / REJECT
---
name: technical-director
description: "High-level technical decisions — engine architecture, technology choices, performance strategy, technical risk, cross-system conflicts."
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, Bash, WebSearch
model: opus
maxTurns: 30
memory: project
---

You are the Technical Director for an indie game project. You own the technical
vision and ensure all code, systems, and tools form a coherent, maintainable,
and performant whole.

### Collaboration Protocol

**You are the highest-level consultant, but the user makes all final strategic decisions.** Your role is to present options, explain trade-offs, and provide expert recommendations — then the user chooses.

#### Strategic Decision Workflow

When the user asks you to make a decision or resolve a conflict:

1. **Understand the full context:**
   - Ask questions to understand all perspectives
   - Review relevant docs (pillars, constraints, prior decisions)
   - Identify what's truly at stake (often deeper than the surface question)

2. **Frame the decision:**
   - State the core question clearly
   - Explain why this decision matters (what it affects downstream)
   - Identify the evaluation criteria (pillars, budget, quality, scope, vision)

3. **Present 2-3 strategic options:**
   - For each option:
     - What it means concretely
     - Which pillars/goals it serves vs. which it sacrifices
     - Downstream consequences (technical, creative, schedule, scope)
     - Risks and mitigation strategies
     - Real-world examples (how other games handled similar decisions)

4. **Make a clear recommendation:**
   - "I recommend Option [X] because..."
   - Explain your reasoning using theory, precedent, and project-specific context
   - Acknowledge the trade-offs you're accepting
   - But explicitly: "This is your call — you understand your vision best."

5. **Support the user's decision:**
   - Once decided, document the decision (ADR, pillar update, vision doc) — ask
     "May I write this to [filepath]?", and do not use Write/Edit until the user has said yes. Ask by ending your turn with the draft and the question; if you are a subagent, whoever called you puts it to the user
   - **Bounded exception — orchestrated runs.** If you were spawned by an orchestrator whose prompt *names the destination path* for this artifact, write it without a separate approval prompt — the user approved the destination when they approved the phase. This holds **only** for a new artifact under `production/`, `docs/` or `tests/`; never an edit to existing source or config, and never a path you chose yourself. If you were invoked directly, or no path was named for you, ask as above.
   - Cascade the decision to affected departments
   - Set up validation criteria: "We'll know this was right if..."

#### Collaborative Mindset

- You provide strategic analysis, the user provides final judgment
- Present options clearly — don't make the user drag it out of you
- Explain trade-offs honestly — acknowledge what each option sacrifices
- Use theory and precedent, but defer to user's contextual knowledge
- Once decided, commit fully — document and cascade the decision
- Set up success metrics — "we'll know this was right if..."

#### Structured Decisions

`AskUserQuestion` is not in your `tools:` grant, so whoever called you presents
your decisions. At each decision point, write the full analysis first (pros/cons,
theory, examples, pillar alignment), then end with the options as a short list:
1-5 word labels, a one-sentence description each (for strategic decisions, the
key trade-off), "(Recommended)" on your pick, at most 4 independent questions.
Open-ended questions and file-write confirmations stay in plain conversation.

### Key Responsibilities

1. **Architecture Ownership**: Define and maintain the high-level system
   architecture. All major systems must have an Architecture Decision Record
   (ADR) approved by you.
2. **Technology Evaluation**: Evaluate and approve all third-party libraries,
   middleware, tools, and engine features before adoption.
3. **Performance Strategy**: Set performance budgets (frame time, memory, load
   times, network bandwidth) and ensure systems respect them.
4. **Technical Risk Assessment**: Identify technical risks early. Maintain a

1	# ADR-0013: Ship Layout Block, Geometry and ID Allocation
2	
3	## Status
4	Proposed
5	
6	## Date
7	2026-10-29
8	
9	## Last Verified
10	2026-10-29 (against `design/gdd/ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-1 to LY-35 and D.5, D.6, D.9, D.10, D.12, D.21; ADR-0001 to ADR-0010, all Proposed; the engine facts marked "probed 2026-10-29" were run on the 4.7.2 mono console binary)
11	
12	## Decision Makers
13	Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.
14	
15	## Summary
16	Ship Section & Layout is the one owner of rooms, rectangles, sockets, welds, bodies and three id spaces, and every Core and Feature system reads or calls it, but no document fixes how its block is shaped, how its rectangles are keyed, how a weld moves a body or which side of the Layout/Graph boundary allocates which id. This ADR decides: `layout.state` stores **instances by reference** to immutable catalog templates as **dense per-column packed arrays** (rows addressed by `id - 1`, tombstones kept, a third persisted `structure_hash` added to the GDD's two); geometry is **integer half-open rectangles** with a flags byte in a reserved, never-renumbered `idx` space; sockets are **sparse terminal-state rows** changed only inside two mutators; weld offsets are computed on the **lower-`body_id` survivor** with a canonicalised `welds[]`; and ids are **split** so that Layout allocates `section_id`, `body_id` and `room_id` from persisted counters while the Graph allocates node, edge, compartment and seam ids and Layout only stores the per-instance bases.
17	
18	## Engine Compatibility
19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (pinned 4.7; installed 4.7.2.stable.mono, `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`) |
23	| **Domain** | Core (simulation data model; scene-tree free, integer-only; the PROJECTOR that draws it is ADR-0034's) |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. The module uses no rendering, physics or scene API. The two HIGH items it touches are the 4.7 packed-array element-write change (every dirty mark here is explicit inside a mutator) and the 4.7 typed-return override rule (it applies to the `@abstract` port of § 8; the rule is sourced from `breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 to 4.7) |
25	| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`; `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows, 4.3 `TileMapLayer` row); `deprecated-apis.md`; `current-best-practices.md` § GDScript (4.7). **`docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` has no core, scripting or tilemap file** (it holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui), so every claim about `Array[String]` encoding, packed-array methods and GDScript cost below is either probed or marked UNVERIFIED. Project ADRs: 0001 to 0010 (§ Related) |
26	| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | Packed-array element writes that skip the property setter (4.7); `@abstract` ports (4.5, chosen by ADR-0010) for `LayoutGraphPort`; typed `Array[String]` as a persisted column. No `TileMapLayer`, `Node` or `Resource` API is used by this ADR |
27	| **Verification Required** | **V1 (probed 2026-10-29, done):** `PackedInt32Array.bsearch(v)` returns the insertion index and, for ties, the first index with `before = true` and one past the last with `before = false`; `PackedInt32Array.insert` and `remove_at` keep order; a value `0xDEADBEEF` stored in a `PackedInt32Array` reads back as `-559038737` and masks to `3735928559`; `var_to_bytes` then `bytes_to_var` returns a typed `Array[String]` still typed and a `PackedInt64Array` exact to 2^40; `PackedStringArray` also round-trips (but ADR-0006 § 1.2 does not allow it in a save, so it is not used); `duplicate()` of a packed array is independent of later element writes. **V2 (UNVERIFIED, spike S1 / SP-ENG-1):** the GDScript cost of the `layout.doors` loop at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` doors on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK against its 0.2 ms line (TR-section-042). **V3 (UNVERIFIED, S1 with ADR-0014):** the P2 cost of `attach_section` and `detach_section` including the per-body broadphase rebuild at `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`. **V4 (UNVERIFIED, after ADR-0005 is Accepted):** golden vectors for `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` and `structure_hash` of the four MVP templates, equal on the editor and on the `template_release` export (ADR-0007 CONTENT-EXP-1). **V5 (UNVERIFIED):** `Array[String]` column cost in `snapshot()` and in the type walk for the largest long-campaign shape of § 12 (tens of rows; expected negligible, measured in SAVE-WRK-1 f) |

30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|-------|-------|
33	| **Depends On** | ADR-0003 (block descriptor, Class A/B mutators, `WriteScope`, fault domains, owner-callable contract); ADR-0004 (dirty-key layout and `KeySpaceDescriptor`); ADR-0005 (canonical encoding, `Hash64.of_value`, `IntMath`, `low32`, block hash cache); ADR-0006 (snapshot types allowed in a save, two-phase `restore`, `ctx.fault`); ADR-0007 (template catalog, manifests, `section_templates` ledger, boot tiers); ADR-0010 (`src/sim/layout/`, ports, lint tiers, `## @hot`); ADR-0001 and ADR-0002 (P2/P3 phases, hook registration, no Layout command). None is Accepted yet, so this ADR cannot be Accepted before them |
34	| **Enables** | ADR-0014 (rect set, broadphase, `OccluderSource`), ADR-0015 (Body consumes `frame_shift`, `moved_sections`, `rects[]`, `section_at`), ADR-0016 (restore order and verifiers over this block), ADR-0017 (Emitter reads `version`/`static_version`, `anchor_geometry`), ADR-0021 (the weld transaction calls LM2/LM3), ADR-0026 (`init_world` calls LM1), ADR-0034 (PROJECTOR inputs and `entity_id` fields), ADR-0020, ADR-0023, ADR-0027 (read views) |
35	| **Blocks** | The Layout epic (template compile and hashes, `layout.state`, LM1 to LM4, `layout.doors`, read views); every Feature story that calls `build_section`, `attach_section`, `detach_section` or reads `rects_in`/`room_at`/`door_passage` |
36	| **Ordering Note** | Wave A. ADR-0011 (Graph data model, same wave) must supply the Graph side of § 3 and § 8: the `instantiate_section` return and its contiguity guarantees, the allocation-free `opening` read and the `LayoutGraphPort` implementation (§ Related lists every assumption). ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016 and ADR-0034 are written afterwards and build on the records fixed here. Where this ADR and the Layout GDD differ (§ Related, "GDD sync"), the ADR is the proposal and the GDD is updated to it, not the reverse |
37	
38	## Context
39	
40	### Problem Statement
41	
42	Layout is the project's single answer to "where is it?". Its GDD (LY-1 to LY-35) fixes behaviour in detail but defers seven implementation questions to ADRs: the block shape against immutable templates (ADR-LAY-01), the id split with the Graph (ADR-LAY-05), the field order of the two template-local byte strings (ADR-LAY-06), and four more that belong to siblings. Three of the deferrals have since been overtaken by Foundation ADRs and no longer mean what the GDD says: ADR-0005 forbids owner-written byte layouts, ADR-0006 limits what a snapshot may contain, and ADR-0003 fixes the shape of a Class A mutator. Without one decision, the Layout epic would invent a snapshot shape the type walk may reject, an id scheme that the Graph's `next_*` counters can desynchronise from, and a weld routine whose result depends on argument order.
43	
44	The decision is needed now because Body, Assembly, Web Map, Emitter and the PROJECTOR all take ids, offsets and rectangle keys from Layout, and a different assumption in any of them (a sparse section id, a body frame origin, a renumbered `idx`) is a save-compatibility defect once the first build leaves the project.
45	
46	### Constraints
47	
48	- **The simulation is pure data** (architecture principle 1): `layout.state` is a `RefCounted` of typed fields and packed arrays; no `Node`, no `Resource`, no float anywhere in the module (LY-3 a, LY-31; ADR-0010 `SIM-01`, `SIM-03`, `SIM-10`).
49	- **Only plain data reaches a save** (ADR-0006 § 1.2 item 3): `null`, `bool`, `int` (64-bit), finite `float`, `String`, `Array`, `Dictionary` with `String` or `int` keys, and `PackedByteArray`/`PackedInt32Array`/`PackedInt64Array`. `PackedStringArray`, `Vector2i`, `Rect2i` and `StringName` are rejected by the walk, although ADR-0005's encoder would accept some of them.
50	- **One encoder, no owner byte writers** (ADR-0005 § 3.1): Layout supplies the shape of a payload and nothing else; `layout_hash()` is the kernel's block hash.
51	- **Every persisted id is a stable string key, a ledger integer or a Graph type id** (ADR-0007 § 3.1); never an array position of another block, never position-derived (registry `position_derived_persisted_id`).
52	- **Content is loaded before the kernel exists** (ADR-0007 § 1.7): templates reach `setup()` as a frozen, get-only `SectionTemplates` catalog; packed arrays are never returned from a catalog (§ 1.5).
53	- **Mutators are Class A with status returns and caller-owned `out` objects** (ADR-0003 § 5); dirty keys are marked explicitly because 4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call a property setter.
54	- **P2 applies commands, P3 runs hooks** (ADR-0001): a hook sees the same tick's P2 state, and the Graph's door `area` and `door_state` change only in P2 (LY-10).
55	- **Capacity ceilings** are fixed by the GDD's Tuning Knobs table and registered constants; this ADR enforces them and does not retype their values.
56	- **Pre-release saves are disposable** (SL-14, ADR-0006 § 2.6); the migration obligation starts when the first build leaves the project, the same moment ADR-0007's ledgers flip to `SHIPPED`.
57	
58	### Requirements
59	
60	- Store instances by reference to templates, with a restore policy that refuses a template edit that would corrupt an instance with history (TR-section-004, -007).
61	- Allocate and never reuse or renumber `section_id`, `body_id`, `room_id`; keep tombstones; persist `graph_ref_base` per instance (TR-section-005, -037).
62	- Express geometry as half-open integer rectangles with a flags byte on the 24-px grid, translation only (TR-section-010).
63	- Keep the door leaf as one rectangle derived from the Graph's `area` in the P3 `layout.doors` hook, with correct seeding, unknown-opening and clamp behaviour (TR-section-012, -013, -014, -034, -035, -042).
64	- Make sockets terminal-state records changed only by LM2/LM3, with a closed first-failure-wins mating predicate (TR-section-018, -019, TR-assembly-025).
65	- Provide exactly four Class A mutators with pure checks, and weld offsets that do not depend on argument order (TR-section-020, -021).
66	- Own room identity, `V` and `exposed_tiles`, own no loose-item table, no `visited` bit, no pose (TR-section-027, -028).
67	- Enforce capacity ceilings and the block-size diagnostic (TR-section-030, TR-derelict-040, TR-webmap-036).
68	- Publish read views with fixed field names and deterministic order, including CONSOLE anchor records (TR-section-039, TR-derelict-034, TR-horror-031, -032).
69	
70	### Binding stances respected (registry check, `docs/registry/architecture.yaml`)
71	
72	| Registered stance | How this ADR conforms |
73	|---|---|
74	| `owner_callable_contract`, `block_registration`, `mutator_status` (ADR-0003) | `layout.state`, `layout.doors`, the fault domain and the key space are registered in `BOOTING` through `ModuleFacet.registrar`; the four mutators are Class A, statuses `OK`/`REFUSED`/`-code`, results through `out`. The `can_*` names diverge from the `check_*` example in the registry; the shape does not (§ 9) |
75	| `dirty_key_marking`, `change_notification` (ADR-0004) | Keys are `(KIND << 32) | id` with kinds SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3 as LY-32 and **one added kind, LEAF 4** (§ 8); `quiet_writes_allowed` is false |
76	| `canonical_encode_and_hash`, `block_persistence_payload` (ADR-0005, ADR-0006) | The snapshot is a `Dictionary` of named packed arrays; no int-keyed dictionary, no `PackedStringArray`; template hashes are `Hash64.of_value` of three sub-payloads whose shape § 4 fixes |
77	| `static_content_catalogs`, `id_ledgers` (ADR-0007) | Templates arrive as a frozen `SectionTemplates` through `setup()`; `section_templates` ledger nesting is decided in § 4 |
78	| `position_derived_persisted_id`, `block_as_resource_or_node`, `live_reference_in_snapshot_payload`, `packed_array_exposed_or_setter_tracked` (forbidden patterns) | No id derives from a position; the block is a `RefCounted`; payload arrays are duplicates; dirty marking is explicit |
79	| `fault_domain_table` | Layout is static domain 4 |
80	
81	No registered stance is contradicted. Three Foundation texts are read as follows and recorded as asks rather than worked around: ADR-0003 § 5 names the pure check `check_*` (this ADR keeps the GDD's published `can_*` names and the same shape), ADR-0005 § 3.2 lists `PackedStringArray` as encodable while ADR-0006 § 1.2 rejects it in a save (this ADR avoids it), and ADR-0007 § 3.2 describes one id range per ledger space (§ 4 uses one range and a class split by key shape).
82	
83	## Decision
84	
85	### Architecture Diagram
86	
87	```
88	 content (before the kernel exists)                       kernel BOOTING (ADR-0003)
89	 ---------------------------------                        ------------------------
90	 assets/data/sections/*.json  --ADR-0007 stage 3-->  SectionTemplates (frozen, get-only)
91	   + ids.lock.json (flat pairs)                         |  compiled rect table, rooms, sockets, doors,
92	   + geometry/visual/structure hashes (once)            |  anchors, slots, 3 hashes per template
93	                                                        v
94	                                         LayoutModule.setup(facet, templates, tuning, graph_port)
95	                                           registers: block layout.state  hook layout.doors
96	                                                      fault domain 4  key space {SEC,BODY,SEAM,LEAF}
97	 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	 RUNNING                             owner object LayoutModule (src/sim/layout/)
99	                                     +------------------------------+     +----------------------------+
100	   Web Map init_world (INIT) ------> | LayoutState  (persisted)     |     | LayoutDerived (RAM only)   |
101	     LM1 build_section               |  counters, bodies, instances,| --> |  row lookups, socket refs, |
102	   Assembly weld apply (P2) -------> |  sockets, welds   (SoA)      |     |  leaf cache, versions,     |
103	     Graph.weld_join -> LM2          +------------------------------+     |  opening_leaves, caps,     |
104	   Assembly cut apply (P2) -------> LM3        ^ snapshot/restore           |  broadphase handle (0014)  |
105	   Web Map discard -----------------> LM4      | (copy into existing object) +----------------------------+
106	   P3 hook layout.doors  <-- Graph.opening(edge) (LayoutGraphPort) : leaf_w = width - floor(width*area/area_max)
107	                                                   |
108	   reads: room_at, section_at, door_passage, anchor_geometry, ...  --> Body, Emitter, Horror, Interaction,
109	          rects_in / solid_in (ADR-0014)                                Failure & Trail, PROJECTOR (ADR-0034)
110	
111	 id split:   Layout   section_id  body_id  room_id      (counters in layout.state, first id 1, dense, never reused)
112	             Graph    node_id  edge_id  compartment_id  seam_id   (counters in graph.state)
113	             bridge   per instance  graph_ref_base {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}  (stored by Layout, returned by Graph M1)
114	```
115	
116	### 1. The block: one `layout.state`, instances by reference, derived state kept apart
117	
118	Layout registers exactly one block, `layout.state`, with the descriptor values of LY-1 and the fields ADR-0003 requires:
119	
120	| `BlockDescriptor` field | Value |
121	|---|---|
122	| `block_id` / `owner_name` | `&"layout.state"` / `&"layout"` |
123	| `schema_version` / `supported_versions` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` (GDD Tuning Knobs, 1) / `[1]` |
124	| `block_class` / `persist` / `persist_scope` / `scope` | `SIM` / true / `WORLD` / `SHARED` |
125	| `gameplay` / `interpolated` | true / false |
126	| `repl_hint` | `SHARED_SUMMARY`: the summary is the instance table plus the three hashes; geometry never travels (templates are identical on every peer by `catalogue_version`) |
127	| `restore_after` | `[]`: Layout is the root of the restore order and reads no other block in `restore()`; ADR-0016 owns the DAG |
128	| `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `post_restore`, `read_view`, `empty_view` | six registered `Callable`s, each ending `return ctx.complete()`; `commit_baseline`/`snap_baseline` absent (not interpolated); `init_world`/`binding_source` absent (Web Map's `init_world` calls LM1; Layout binds nothing) |
129	
130	**Instances by reference (ADR-LAY-01).** A template is authored, immutable and lives in the frozen `SectionTemplates` catalog; an instance is a row in `layout.state` that names a template by its `template_id` string and carries only what can differ between two instances of one template: its ids, body, offset, id bases, drift hashes and socket/weld history. Full geometry in the block would multiply rectangles by sections, duplicate authored data, defeat the Vertical Slice "seed plus deltas" model and let an exporter bug corrupt the world permanently; a second `layout.templates` block would add a second restore root for nothing. Both are rejected (§ Alternatives 1 and 2).
131	
132	**Two objects, one owner.** The module owns two plain `RefCounted` objects:
133	
134	- **`LayoutState`** holds the persisted tables of § 2 as typed fields. It is the object the block descriptor's callables read and write; `restore` copies into it and never replaces it (ADR-0003 § 2), because the read-view facade `LayoutViews` wraps it for the life of the process.
135	- **`LayoutDerived`** holds everything that is rebuilt from `LayoutState`, the templates and the Graph and is **never snapshotted or hashed**: the `section_id`-indexed lookup columns, the socket-ref index, the live-count caps, the leaf cache and `opening_leaves` map (§ 8), the three version counters and `changed_region` stamps (§ 7), `mutation_count`, and the handle to ADR-0014's broadphase. The split is what makes "derived caches are never persisted" (TR-section-004) checkable: a test snapshots `LayoutState` only, and the allow-list test of AC-130 walks only that payload.
136	
137	**What the block never holds.** Floats; geometry; the section `kind` (the Graph's section record owns it, LS-17); a `visited` bit (the block is WORLD-scoped and rolls back on `request_restore`); a loose-item table (Interaction's `interaction.state` holds it and lists `layout.state` in its own `restore_after`); a door `area` or `door_state`; atmosphere; pose, velocity or any `body.state` field; a stored `layout_hash` or `mutation_count` (Save/Load's `block_state_hash` owns the stored copy, LY D.10, OQ-36). This is TR-section-028 and the first half of TR-section-013.
138	
139	**Source layout (ADR-0010).** `src/sim/layout/`: `layout_module.gd` (owner, registration, callables), `layout_state.gd`, `layout_derived.gd`, `layout_ids.gd`, `socket_ref.gd`, `layout_faults.gd`, `layout_mutators.gd` (LM1 to LM4 and checks), `weld_math.gd` and `detach_planner.gd` (pure), `door_leaves.gd` (the hook), `layout_restore.gd` (validation), `views/` (`LayoutViews` and the record classes of § 11), `ports/layout_graph_port.gd` (`@abstract`, § 8). The PROJECTOR is `src/presentation/projector/` and is never imported from here. The pure compile of authored runs into the rect table (`TemplateCompiler`) lives under `src/data/sections/` beside the loader that calls it, owned by Layout by review, not by import (ADR-0007 § 1.9).
140	
141	### 2. The snapshot payload: dense parallel columns, ascending ids, tombstones kept
142	
143	`snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload)` with a `Dictionary` whose keys are `String`s. Every table is a set of **parallel columns** (TR-section-006): no `Dictionary` is keyed by an id, no `Vector2i`/`Rect2i`/`Color`/`Resource`/`StringName`, no `PackedStringArray`, and every packed array in the payload is a `duplicate()` (ADR-0003 snapshot contract; registry `live_reference_in_snapshot_payload`). The key set is closed; the AC-130 allow-list file is regenerated from this table.
144	
145	| Payload key | Type | Contents (row order) |
146	|---|---|---|
147	| `schema_version` | `int` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` |
148	| `counters` | `Dictionary` of three `int`s | `next_section_id`, `next_body_id`, `next_room_id` (first allocated id is 1, so `default_state` sets all three to 1) |
149	| `bodies` | `Dictionary` | `body_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `origin_section_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `state` (`PackedByteArray`: 0 `LIVE`, 1 `DISSOLVED`); ascending `body_id` |
150	| `instances` | `Dictionary` of 14 columns | `section_id`, `body_id`, `offset_x`, `offset_y`, `room_id_base`, `node_base`, `edge_base`, `comp_base`, `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash`, `structure_hash` (all `PackedInt32Array`); `rot_q`, `discarded` (`PackedByteArray`); `template_id` (`Array[String]`); ascending `section_id` |
151	| `sockets` | `Dictionary` | `section_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `socket_index` (`PackedByteArray`), `state` (`PackedByteArray`: 1 `WELDED`, 2 `CAPPED`, 3 `CUT_OPEN`; `FREE` = 0 is never stored), `seam_id` (`PackedInt32Array`); ascending `(section_id, socket_index)`; only non-`FREE` sockets have a row |
152	| `welds` | `Dictionary` | `seam_id`, `section_a`, `section_b` (`PackedInt32Array`), `socket_a`, `socket_b`, `state` (`PackedByteArray`; `state`: 0 `ACTIVE`, 1 `CUT_SEALED`, 2 `CUT_RAGGED`), `welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T` (`PackedInt64Array`); ascending `seam_id` |
153	
154	Decisions inside the shape:
155	
156	- **Ids are dense ordinals: `section_id == row + 1` and `body_id == row + 1`.** A section or body id is consumed only by the mutator that appends its row, in the same call, so no id exists without a row. Row lookup is then an index, not a map: no `Dictionary` on the read path, no `bsearch` for the common query. Restore verifies the equality (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`). The cost is that a future "reserve an id then maybe not use it" idea is forbidden by this ADR, which is the right pressure (§ Risks R1).
157	- **`template_id` is a typed `Array[String]` column** (TR-section-004). The alternatives were the ledger integer (rejected: the GDD allow-list, LY-6 b and every restore reason name the string; four templates; saves are disposable pre-release; a human-readable dump matters more than 4 bytes a row) and a `PackedStringArray` (rejected: not on ADR-0006's allow-list). **Probed 2026-10-29:** a typed `Array[String]` survives `var_to_bytes`/`bytes_to_var` still typed.
158	- **64-bit times are native `PackedInt64Array` columns** (TR-section-006). ADR-0006 § 1.2 item 3 allows full-width `int` and § 1.3 limits the halves convention to values that can reach JSON; `welded_at_T`/`cut_at_T` reach JSON only through the dev `dump-save`, which renders any `int` of magnitude 2^53 or more as a decimal string and `T` is bounded below 2^53. The GDD's two-halves form stays legal and is not used.
159	- **The three hashes are stored as signed int32 and compared as `value & 0xFFFFFFFF`** (`IntMath.low32`, ADR-0005 P9; probed 2026-10-29). A comparison without the mask is a lint-visible defect (AC-172 c).
160	- **`rot_q` is a byte column that must be 0.** It is stored so the field exists in schema v1 and a later rotation feature is not a layout change; any nonzero value is `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED` at restore and a boot error in a template that asks for it.
161	- **`socket_index` is the template's declaration ordinal** of that socket, a `uint8` (MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION never exceeds 8 and is lint-bounded by `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION`). A runtime socket handle is the packed int `SocketRef = (section_id << 4) | socket_index` (`socket_ref.gd`, 24 bits at the section-id ceiling), used as an argument, a memo key and a sort key; it is never persisted.
162	- **Seam ids are the Graph's.** A `welds` row's `seam_id` is whatever `weld_join` returned; Layout allocates none and treats it as an opaque positive `int32`. After a cut the two sockets keep their `seam_id` (state `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN`) because the scar's bead and cap plate are drawn from that history (Pillar 5).
163	- **The payload size rule holds.** The largest realistic shape (D.21's long campaign) is tens of KB, far under `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`; `snapshot()` computes the D.21 estimate from row counts and raises the one-shot diagnostic `layout_block_soft_bytes` when it exceeds `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` (GDD Tuning Knobs); the hard ceiling is Save/Load's (TR-section-030).
164	
165	**Tombstones.** A discarded section keeps its row with `discarded = 1` and its `body_id`; the body it sat on becomes `DISSOLVED`; its `socket` and `welds` rows stay (a surviving mate keeps its `CAPPED`/`CUT_OPEN` history). Ids stay consumed, so nothing is ever reused or renumbered (TR-section-005).
166	
167	### 3. ID allocation and the split with the Graph (ADR-LAY-05)
168	
169	| Id | Allocator | Counter and home | Range and rule |
170	|---|---|---|---|
171	| `section_id` | **Layout** | `next_section_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^20 - 1` so `rect_key` fits 32 bits (D.9); `can_build` returns `CAPACITY` before consuming `2^20` |
172	| `body_id` | **Layout** | `next_body_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^31 - 1` (int32 column); one new id per LM1 and per LM3 |
173	| `room_id` | **Layout** | `next_room_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^31 - 1`; **contiguous per instance**: `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`, `room_index` the room's declaration order in the template |
174	| `node_id`, `edge_id`, `compartment_id` | **Graph** | `next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, comp counter in `graph.state` | returned by M1 as `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` and stored by Layout per instance as `graph_ref_base` |
175	| `seam_id`, opening ids | **Graph** | `next_seam_id` in `graph.state` | given to Layout in LM2's arguments and read back through `seam_view` |
176	| `section_id` in `graph.state` | follows Layout | `next_section_id` in `graph.state` | M1 advances it to `max(section_id) + 1`; Layout never reads it except in the post-restore verification |
177	
178	**Mapping rules (all derived, none persisted).**
179	
180	- Template-local index to Graph id: `node_id = node_base + node_ref_index`, `edge_id = edge_base + edge_ref_index`; template-local room to compartment: `comp_id = comp_base + room_index`; room to id: `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`. Hence `compartment_of_room(room_id) = comp_base(section) + (room_id - room_id_base(section))` and the inverse.
181	- Reverse lookup (a Graph id or a `room_id` to its section) is a `bsearch` over the ascending base column (`node_base`, `edge_base`, `comp_base`, `room_id_base` are all ascending because every allocator is monotone and rows append). A section whose range does not contain the id answers `NONE` (a discarded section's `anchor_geometry` answers nothing, without an error, FT:703).
182	- These rules require the Graph to return **contiguous** node, edge and compartment ranges **in template order** from M1 (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011) and to size each range from the template alone, so the post-restore check "node, edge and compartment counts match the template" is a pure comparison.
183	
184	**When ids are consumed.** LM1 reads (does not yet advance) `next_section_id`, `next_body_id` and `next_room_id`, calls the Graph's M1 with the section id, and only on an `OK` status appends the rows and advances the counters. So a Graph defect leaves Layout's counters and tables untouched (fail-closed per ADR-0003 § 5; the kernel is `FAULTED` anyway). `can_build` and `can_detach` test every counter ceiling **before** any id is consumed or the Graph is called, so no counter ever wraps (TR-section-037).
185	
186	**Why Layout owns the section id.** The Graph's M1 takes "a caller section id" (LS-15, LS-19), the Graph's `next_section_id` then follows Layout's, and Layout needs the section id to exist before the Graph does (it keys the dirty key and the body row). The alternative of the Graph allocating it (§ Alternatives 4) would make Layout's `build_section` depend on a return value to name its own row and would put the `rect_key` bound (2^20) in the Graph's hands.
187	
188	### 4. Template identity, the ledger nesting (OQ-B) and the three hashes (ADR-LAY-04, -06)
189	
190	**Ledger nesting (ADR-0007 OQ-B).** `assets/data/sections/ids.lock.json` is one `section_templates` space with one flat `pairs[]`, exactly the shape ADR-0007 § 3.2 defines, so `LedgerCheck.verify` stays generic and the append-only CI gate needs no second format. Two classes share the space, told apart by **key shape**: a template pair has key `<template_id>`, a room pair has key `<template_id>/<room_key>` (the `/` is illegal inside a snake_case key, so the split is unambiguous). Template ids come from the low part of the declared range and room ids from above a fixed boundary (a `SectionLedgerCheck` in `src/data/sections/`, owned by Layout by review, checks the boundary, that every room pair's prefix is a template pair in the same ledger, and that retiring or dormanting a template does the same to its room pairs: lint `LEDGER_ROOM_ORPHAN`). One entry per `room_key` rather than a nested list keeps `dormant` and `retired_ids` per room, so removing one room from a template is a per-pair `dormant` flip and a renamed room is a visible new pair, which is the diff a migration step needs. The integers are **not persisted in `layout.state`** (the instance persists the `template_id` string, § 2); they exist so a rename or removal after `SHIPPED` is detected and migrated (ADR-0007 § 3.3), and so later blocks can reference a room by integer if they must.
191	
192	**The three hashes (the shape of ADR-LAY-06).** ADR-0005 § 3.1 forbids an owner-written `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` byte string, and § 4.6 already defines the template hashes as `Hash64.of_value` of a post-cast sub-payload "whose shape is Layout's and ADR-0013's". So ADR-LAY-06 becomes the **`Dictionary` shape of three sub-payloads**, hashed once by `SectionTemplates` at catalog freeze and stored as `low32` in the template row (never in the template file, ADR-0007 § 3.5):
193	
194	| Hash | Payload (keys sorted by the encoder, so order in source is irrelevant; every family is one flat `PackedInt32Array` in the field order of its LY-4 row, strings replaced by template-local indices, variable-length members as a CSR `*_off` array plus a data array) | Changes when |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `geometry_hash` | `size_tiles`; `rooms` (origin, flags, tile runs); `wall_runs` (orientation, start, length, kind, flanking rooms, `face_h_px`, `face_variant`); the compiled `rects` (stride 7: `x0, y0, x1, y1, flags, owner_kind, owner_ref`, in `idx` order, leaf and variant slots at their closed or full extent); `doors`; `sockets` with their `lanes`; `hardpoints`; `plate_positions`; `loose_slots`; `story_slots`; `anchors` (polyline CSR); `fixture_anchors`; `instrument_placements` (geometry fields only) | anything that decides where a rectangle, tile, socket, door or anchor is |
197	| `visual_hash` | `dialect`; kit-piece ids and layers; art references; labels; advisory hints (`socket_tag`); flags no query reads | only presentation changes |
198	| `structure_hash` | the **ordered** key sequences: `room_key[]`, `socket_key[]`, `door_key[]`, `hp_key[]`, `node_ref[]`, `edge_ref[]`, `anchor_key[]`, `slot_id[]`; each room's sorted tile list | any reorder, add, remove or rename of an identity-bearing element, or any tile-set change |
199	
200	**Why a third hash.** LY-26 e classifies a template change as "structural" when the *sets* of keys or a room's tile set differ, but the block persists only two hashes, so the check has nothing to compare against except Graph counts. A pure **reordering** (rooms `[a, b]` to `[b, a]`) keeps every set equal and every count equal, yet `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`, `socket_index` and `comp_base + room_index` all index the *current* template by position, so an existing save would silently attach its Graph compartments and welded sockets to the wrong rooms and sockets. LY-6 e's sentence "a template that merely reorders rooms changes ids only for NEW instances" is therefore wrong as written. The remedy is to persist what the check needs: `structure_hash` is one more `int32` per instance (§ 2), costs four bytes a row, and makes the structural rule exact: **a `structure_hash` mismatch is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` for every instance, history or not**, because every instance has Graph data built from the old order. `geometry_hash` keeps the GDD's history-dependent rule (§ 10). The third hash is not redundant with `geometry_hash`: because `rooms` are encoded in declaration order, a reorder already changes `geometry_hash`, which on an instance **with history** is refused by the GDD's own rule; the marginal value of `structure_hash` is the **never-welded `FREE` instance**, where the history-dependent rule would accept the change as `geometry_changed_fresh` and silently re-point `room_id_base + room_index`, `comp_base + room_index` and `socket_index` to the wrong rooms and sockets. This is a deliberate deviation from the TR text "13-int section-instance rows" (the row is 14 columns, one of them the string); it is listed first among the decisions for the user's review.
201	
202	**Two more template rules.** (a) Every coordinate of a footprint rectangle, socket `line_px`/`start_px`, room `origin_px` and wall run lies on the 24-px grid (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`) except a door leaf's moving edge (LY-3 a, LY-7); `GRID_24` is a **BOOT invariant** (`CONTENT_INVARIANT`, ADR-0007 § 2.4), not only a CI lint, because the closure of the weld offset on the grid (§ 7) and the broadphase cell alignment depend on it; a 12-px shift in a socket fails the load (TR-derelict-033 Layout half). (b) `area_max <= 0` on a door is the one named structural invariant D.5 needs (it divides by it) and refuses the load; the published `area_max` range is guidance (ADR-0007 § 2.5).
203	
204	### 5. Rectangles, units and frames: the record, the flags and the reserved `idx` space
205	
206	ADR-0014 owns the broadphase, `QueryBuffer`, `OccluderSource` and the query signatures. This ADR owns **what a rectangle is, how it is keyed and which ones can exist**.
207	
208	- **The record (TR-section-010).** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, **half-open** `[x0, x1) x [y0, y1)` over pixel cells, with one flags byte: `SOLID`, `OCCLUDES_LIGHT`, `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL` (registry `layout_rect_flags`). The legal flag combinations are LY-7's table and a boot error otherwise (`RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`). A rect with `x1 <= x0` or `y1 <= y0` is omitted from every result but keeps its `idx`.
209	- **Units and frames.** The unit is the base pixel; `TILE_PX` is the floor tile and `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` the wall depth. There is no world frame in Layout. Reads answer **section-local** except those that answer for one body (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `section_at`, `weld_offset`, `detach_preview`), which answer in the **body frame** = section-local + `offset_px(section_id)` (LY-3 c).
210	- **Transforms are integer translation only.** No rotation, no mirror, no zoom value appears anywhere in Layout (LY-3 d, e). Every px-to-tile or px-to-cell conversion is **floor** division through `IntMath.floor_div` (body-frame coordinates may be negative after a detach re-base); the bare `/` and `%` operators appear nowhere in `src/sim/layout/` (ADR-0010 `SIM-05`).
211	- **The `idx` space is compiled once per template and never changes** (D.9): static rects sorted by `(y0, x0, y1, x1, flags)` are `0 .. N_static - 1`; one reserved leaf slot per door follows in door declaration order; two reserved variant slots (PLATE, JAMB) per **hatched** socket follow, `idx = N_static + N_doors + 2h + v`. The key `(section_id, idx)` is therefore stable across attach, detach, restore and animation: a state change only switches slots between active and inactive; an inactive or zero-length slot is omitted from results and keeps its `idx` (TR-section-020's "renumbers nothing" half).
212	- **Rect keys.** `rect_key = section_id * RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` with the stride `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` (GDD Tuning Knobs, a power of two) and `idx < stride`; the key reaches `2^32 - 1`, so every key column is `PackedInt64Array` (ADR-0014 owns the buffer). Boot refuses a template whose `N_static + N_doors + 2 N_hatched` exceeds the stride (`RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW`).
213	- **The compiled table is catalog data.** `SectionTemplate` exposes rect `idx`-indexed accessors (`rect_count()`, `rect_x0(i)`, `rect_y0(i)`, `rect_x1(i)`, `rect_y1(i)`, `rect_flags(i)`, `rect_owner_kind(i)`, `rect_owner_ref(i)`), never a packed array (ADR-0007 § 1.5). The bulk read that builds a body's grid at build, attach, detach and restore is ADR-0014's; those events are cold, so accessor calls are acceptable there (V3 measures them).
214	- **Static footprint set versus query set.** `rects_in` returns `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rects and `solid_in` returns `SOLID` rects in their *current leaf state*; the mating overlap test of § 6 uses the **static** set with all flags, so a door animating can never flip a verdict. Both sets are views of one rect set (Pillar 1: collision, light and drawing cannot disagree); neither is an engine collision shape, and the avatar has no physics body.

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.
