216	### 6. Sockets, seams and the mating predicate
217	
218	- **A socket is a pre-declared attachment site** `{socket_key, facing N|E|S|W, line_px, start_px, width_tiles, class_id, lanes[], hatch | none}` in the template (LY-13). `pos_px` is `(line_px, start_px)` for E/W facings and `(start_px, line_px)` for N/S. The four-facing footprint, LOW-end, PLATE/JAMB/LEAF table of LY-13 is normative and is not restated.
219	- **States (TR-section-018, TR-assembly-025).** `FREE -> WELDED(seam_id) -> CAPPED` (after a SEALED cut) or `CUT_OPEN` (after a RAGGED cut); `CAPPED` and `CUT_OPEN` never return to `FREE` in MVP, which supports exactly one weld-then-cut cycle per socket. **A socket's state is written only inside LM2 and LM3.** There is no `install_cap_plate`, no `set_socket_state` and no setter on `LayoutState.sockets`; `socket_state` writes are private to `weld_math`/`detach_planner` helpers called by those two mutators, and a lint (`LAY-SOCKET-01`, tier E1, ADR-0010 § 6) rejects any other write to the `sockets` columns.
220	- **`can_attach` is a pure, first-failure-wins reason chain** (TR-section-019), cheap before expensive, in this fixed order: `SOCKET_UNKNOWN`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `SAME_BODY`, `FACING_MISMATCH`, `WIDTH_MISMATCH`, `CLASS_MISMATCH`, `LANE_MISMATCH`, `GEOM_OVERLAP`. `SAME_BODY` being a hard reject and every weld merging two bodies is what makes the weld relation a **forest** and a cut always split a body into exactly two components.
221	- **`GEOM_OVERLAP`.** The test set is the static footprint of both bodies after the D.6 translation: every static rect with all flags, each PLATE slot at its full footprint, no leaf and no JAMB slot, plus the tile cells of every room (rect against tile and tile against tile, so a wall over the other body's floor and two floors on one cell both fail); abutting is legal. It runs over each body's broadphase handle (ADR-0014) and is **memoised on `(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)`**; uncached cost target <= 2 ms (TR-section-019), a pending-spike figure (V3). The memo is a small fixed-capacity ring in `LayoutDerived`, reset on restore.
222	- **Slot activation is a pure function** of `(this socket's state, this socket's hatch, the mate's hatch, W)` evaluated by LM1 to LM4 and `post_restore` (the LY-15 matrix); no persisted field is needed because the mate's hatch is known from the two templates. A hatched socket whose mate is bare is `hatch_one_sided`: legal, behaves bulkhead-only, its PLATE stays on while `WELDED`.
223	- **The `can_attach` preview needs more than a reason**, and a Class A check returns a bare `StringName` (ADR-0003 § 5). So the payload `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}` is its own pure read, `preview_attach(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: AttachPreview) -> void`, and `can_attach(...)` is `preview_attach` followed by returning `out.reason` (`&""` = OK). One implementation, two shapes.
224	- **`socket_plan(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: WeldPlan)`** is a pure read that fills the Graph's weld-plan DATA verbatim (one lane pair per lane in `(loop, lane_index)` order, one opening per mated hatch pair `(comp_a, comp_b, area_max)`, `L_seam = width_tiles`). The field layout of `WeldPlan` follows ADR-0011's `JoinPlan`; Layout fills it, Assembly adds `q`, the Graph's `can_join` validates, and both verdicts must pass before apply.
225	
226	### 7. Weld offsets, bodies and the detach re-base
227	
228	**Bodies.** `bodies[]` is Layout's: `{body_id, origin_section_id, state}`. **Every built section starts on its own new body at offset (0, 0), and every multi-section body is produced by welds only** (LY-25): there is no "place on an existing body" path, so the forest property holds by construction. A body's frame origin is the origin of its `origin_section_id`.
229	
230	**Weld offset (D.6, TR-section-021).** `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b`, where `a` is the **survivor-side** socket and `b` the absorbed-side socket, assigned **by body, never by argument order**: the body with the **lower `body_id`** survives (the older body; the home ship in the MVP). `attach_section` re-labels the two arguments internally, so `attach_section(x, y, ...)` and `attach_section(y, x, ...)` produce the same survivor, the same `offset_b`, the same `frame_shift_px`, and a **byte-identical** `layout.state`: the `welds[]` row always records the survivor-side section and socket as `section_a`/`socket_a` (canonicalisation). `weld_math.gd` is a pure module of integer helpers (`survivor_of`, `offset_b`, `frame_shift`) with no state, which `weld_offset(...)` (the pure read), `can_attach` and LM2 all call, so prediction and apply cannot drift.
231	
232	**24-grid closure.** `pos_a`, `pos_b` and `offset_a` lie on the 24-px grid (`GRID_24` is a boot invariant, § 4), and `offset_a` does by induction from (0, 0), so `offset_b` does; an off-grid `offset_b` from a validated plan is therefore a **defect**, not a reason code: `apply` raises `LAYOUT_OFFSET_OFF_GRID` (domain 4) and returns its negative.
233	
234	**LM2 effects, in order** (all inside the caller's single P2 apply, after the Graph's `weld_join`): append the `welds[]` row (`ACTIVE`); upsert both socket rows to `WELDED(seam_id)` keeping ascending order; shift every section of the absorbed body by `frame_shift_px = offset_b - offset_b_old` and move it to the survivor `body_id`; mark the absorbed body `DISSOLVED`; switch the PLATE/JAMB/LEAF slots of both sockets (§ 6); seed each newly active LEAF **closed** with its last-projected cache (§ 8); rebuild the affected broadphase handles (ADR-0014); bump `static_version` and `version` of **every section whose socket state changed (including the host section that does not move) and every moved section**; stamp `changed_region` (REGION for the two socket-host sections, FRAME for the other moved sections); cache the mated hatch's opening ids from `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]` into `opening_leaves`; mark `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<survivor>`, `BODY/<absorbed>` and `SEC/<id>` for each affected section (5 keys for the MVP weld of two single-section bodies). The returned `AttachResult` carries `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}`; `body_of` of every moved section is the survivor in the same apply and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick.
235	
236	**LM3 and the detach re-base (D.12).** After the Graph's `cut_detach`, LM3 marks the weld row `CUT_SEALED` or `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`; sets both sockets `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` (keeping `seam_id`); then **enumerates the connected components of the `ACTIVE` weld forest minus the cut seam, in ascending `section_id`**. The component containing the body's `origin_section_id` keeps its `body_id`; the other receives a new `body_id` from `next_body_id`, its `origin_section_id` is `m`, the minimum `section_id` of that component, and its offsets are re-based by `frame_shift = offset_old(m)` (`offset_new(s) = offset_old(s) - frame_shift`). The traversal uses preallocated `PackedInt32Array` stack and visited columns in `LayoutDerived`, bounded by `MAX_SECTIONS`, so no container is built in the apply. `DetachPlanner.plan(...)` is the single implementation behind both `detach_preview(seam_id)` and LM3, so the preview and the apply cannot drift (Assembly's `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT`). A cut that does not yield exactly two components is a defect (`LAYOUT_COMPONENT_COUNT`), unreachable by the forest argument. The `DetachResult` is `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}` with `rects[]` the cut seam's two hatch rectangles in the pre-cut body frame, **computed before the sockets change**, exactly equal to `detach_preview(seam_id).rects`. Layout performs **no actor check** (it reads nothing from `body.state`): the CHANNEL path is vetoed by Assembly's completion validate, and Body's `rebase_on_detach` is the net behind it (LY-17, BDY-24 iii).
237	
238	**Why not argument order or "the larger body".** Argument order makes the dissolved body depend on a caller's mixup (the home ship could dissolve) and makes the block bytes differ between two equal worlds, which breaks AC-172 (equal blocks by different histories hash equal). "Larger body survives" would make survival depend on a count that changes with every weld. The lower `body_id` is a persisted, immutable, total order.
239	
240	### 8. The door leaf, the `layout.doors` hook and the Graph port
241	
242	**One rectangle per leaf.** A door or hatch has one leaf rect. With `width_px` (the 96-px door cell), the Graph opening's `area` clamped to `[0, area_max]` and `area_max > 0`: `gap = floor_div(width_px * area, area_max)`, `leaf_w = width_px - gap`, and the rect is anchored to the hinge side with depth `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (D.5; hinge LOW for every socket hatch so both leaves of a mated hatch retract the same way). `leaf_w = 0` returns no rect and keeps its `idx`. A mated hatch is two leaves (one per section) driven by one `area`.
243	
244	**The port.** Layout reads and calls the Graph only through `LayoutGraphPort` (`src/sim/layout/ports/layout_graph_port.gd`, `@abstract`, ADR-0010 § 3), implemented by the Graph's facade and injected into `setup()`:
245	
246	```gdscript
247	@abstract class_name LayoutGraphPort extends RefCounted
248	@abstract func check_instantiate(views: SimViews, template_id: String) -> StringName   # Graph CAPACITY pre-check for can_build
249	@abstract func instantiate_section(scope: WriteScope, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int, out: SectionBases) -> int
250	@abstract func opening_into(edge_id: int, out: OpeningRead) -> bool   # false = unknown edge; fills area, area_max, door_state
251	@abstract func seam_openings_into(seam_id: int, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool   # opening_ids[] in socket_plan.openings order
252	@abstract func section_counts_into(section_id: int, out: SectionCounts) -> bool   # nodes, edges, compartments, next_section_id (verification only)
253	```
254	
255	The 4.7 typed-return rule applies to any override of a typed-return abstract method, so each implementation returns explicitly on every path (a stub that omits a return is a parse error or a defect found by V-lint). The reads are allocation-free (caller-owned `out`), valid in P3 and in P2 after the Graph's own writes.
256	
257	**The hook (TR-section-012).** `layout.doors`: `hook_id &"layout.doors"`, owner Layout, `divisor 1`, `offset 0`, `after []`, running in P3. Body's `body.integrate` is registered `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]` (BDY-8), which orders the Emitter after it transitively, so every P3 reader sees same-tick leaves. The hook loops over the `LayoutDerived` leaf cache, a dense list of at most `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` slots in ascending `(section_id, door_index)` (deterministic bump order):
258	
259	1. `graph.opening_into(edge, op)`. If it returns false (unknown opening) the leaf stays at its last projected value (closed at the template default), `area` is never invented, `leaf_version` is not bumped, and the diagnostic `opening_unknown` is raised **once per edge** (a bit in the slot's flags, cleared when the read succeeds again) (TR-section-035). A `area_max <= 0` read is treated the same way and counted `opening_invalid`.
260	2. `area` is clamped to `[0, area_max]`; a value above `area_max` raises the diagnostic `area_clamped` and uses `area_max` (TR-section-035).
261	3. `leaf_w` is computed (integer, `IntMath.floor_div`), compared with the slot's last-projected value, and if different the leaf rect is recomputed and the slot's section is flagged.
262	4. After the loop, for each flagged section in ascending id: `leaf_version += 1`, `version += 1`, never `static_version`; `changed_region` is stamped REGION(union of the old and new leaf rectangles). **At most one bump per section per tick** (TR-section-042).
263	5. If any section was flagged, the hook opens `layout.state` once (`scope.open_for`) and marks one **`LEAF/<section_id>`** key per flagged section.
264	
265	**Why the hook marks a key, and why a new kind.** `layout.doors` changes only derived caches, yet the PROJECTOR must redraw a leaf whose rect changed and the door leaf sprite extent must equal the leaf rect with no tween (TR-section-013). ADR-0009 presenters draw from dirty batches; polling every section's counter every frame would add a read per frame for an event that happens a few times per play. Marking is legal (ADR-0004 § 7: a key marked for an unchanged value is not a violation; the HOOK scope may open any block). Its cost is that a granted `open_for` advances `touch_serial`, invalidating the block hash cache (ADR-0005 § 5.2) on those ticks; under the binary door model that is a few ticks per play, and the re-encode is bounded by the block size (tens of KB). LY-32's closed list is SEC, BODY, SEAM; a leaf change under `SEC/<id>` would also wake Failure & Trail's anchor rebuild and Lighting's static rebuild on every door toggle, so the key family **`LEAF` (kind 4)** is added to Layout's own key space (ADR-0004 § 3 leaves unnumbered families to the owner). Subscribers that care (the PROJECTOR, Lighting's dynamic leaf patch) test `batch.has(key)`; the rest ignore it.
266	
267	**The correctness condition.** Every `area` write of a template door or mated hatch lands in **P2** by command (a SYSTEM-origin `set_opening` re-submitted each tick by Interaction's `attempts[]` for a `CLOSING_BLOCKED` retry); no Graph phase writes `area` or `door_state` of such an opening (the Graph's virtual breach and seam-weep openings have no leaf and are neither read nor projected). Layout stores, mirrors and writes neither value (TR-section-013); `layout_hash` does not cover door state. This is a cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011/0012/0020 and a test (AC "closed leaf blocks and an open one does not in the same tick its state changes").
268	
269	**Seeding.** LM1 reads the just-created openings through the port and derives each leaf immediately (the Graph holds authored initial areas), so there is no tick in which a built door is wrong. **LM2 does not read the Graph's `area`:** it initialises each newly active LEAF **closed** (`leaf_w = width_px`) and seeds the last-projected cache with that value in the same apply, because `weld_join` starts the new opening at `area` 0; reads between the P2 apply and the first P3 hook therefore see a solid span, raise no `stale_leaf`, and the hook bumps `leaf_version` only if its `area` read differs (TR-section-034). `post_restore` derives all leaves in one `derive_doors` pass (§ 10).
270	
271	**Pure leaf queries.** `leaf_would_overlap(opening_edge_id, area, boxes: PackedInt32Array) -> bool` and `leaf_obstruction_into(opening_edge_id, area, boxes, out: LeafObstruction) -> bool` evaluate **every** leaf projected from that opening (`opening_leaves`: both sections of a mated hatch) at the new `area`, in the body frame, against every caller-supplied foot box (`boxes` is a flat half-open `x0, y0, x1, y1` array the caller owns); Layout reads nothing from `body.state` (TR-section-014). `door_passage_into(section_id, via_id, out: DoorPassage) -> bool` returns `{orientation, sill_rect, gap_rect, open_extent_px}` from the leaf value `layout.doors` last projected (so collision, light and passage cannot disagree and `opening` is not re-read); an unknown or discarded section or `via_id` returns false with no error; before `post_restore` it reports `open_extent_px` 0 and raises `stale_leaf`. The single passability rule is a pure helper `DoorPassage.passable(open_extent_px, orientation, foot_extent_ew, foot_extent_ns)`: passable iff `open_extent_px` is at least the foot extent across the doorway (the Body foot box, BDY-14: 16 across an east-west run, 8 across a north-south run, supplied by Body as constants, not owned here) (TR-horror-032).
272	
273	**Cost.** The hook is an integer multiply and divide per door plus one port call and compare. Target <= 0.2 ms at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` animating doors (5 percent of `STEP_BUDGET_MS`) on a release export, a pending-spike figure (V2). The fallback ladder is ADR-0010 § 9: cache accessors in locals, then early-out on an unchanged Graph `touch` counter if ADR-0011 publishes one, before any native rung.

314	### 10. Restore, drift and `post_restore`
315	
316	**`restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` is two-phase** (ADR-0003 § 2, ADR-0006 § 2.2): decode and validate into a `LayoutScratch` (cold path, allocation allowed); on any failure call `ctx.fault(code, detail)` and write nothing; on success **copy the contents into the existing `LayoutState` object** (each column assigned from the scratch's own arrays, none aliasing `data`), then rebuild the static `LayoutDerived` (lookups, socket index, caps, version counters reset to 1, `mutation_count` 0, memo cleared, broadphase handles rebuilt by ADR-0014's call). A restore swaps whole tables only on success (TR-section-007).
317	
318	**Validation, in order** (first failure wins, with a named detail): (1) `stored_version` in `supported_versions` and the key set equals the § 2 table, every column has the declared type and equal row counts per table (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_SCHEMA`); (2) every `template_id` resolves in the catalog (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE`); (3) `rot_q` all 0 (`LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`); (4) the drift policy below (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`); (5) dense ids: `section_id[i] == i + 1`, `body_id[i] == i + 1`, `room_id_base[i + 1] == room_id_base[i] + rooms(template[i])`, counters equal the dense count + 1 and below the ceilings (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`); (6) references: every non-discarded instance sits on a `LIVE` body, every `LIVE` body has an in-range `origin_section_id` that belongs to it, socket rows are strictly ascending with `socket_index < template.socket_count` and a resolving `seam_id`, weld rows ascend and agree with their socket states (`ACTIVE` with two `WELDED`, `CUT_SEALED` with two `CAPPED`, `CUT_RAGGED` with two `CUT_OPEN`), `ACTIVE` welds form a forest whose components are exactly the `LIVE` bodies' section sets, and every `ACTIVE` weld's offsets satisfy `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b` on the 24 grid (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING`). An unsupported `stored_version` is a reported failure, never a silent default.
319	
320	**Drift policy (TR-section-007).** The current template's three hashes are compared with the stored ones after `& 0xFFFFFFFF`. A **`structure_hash`** difference is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` for every instance (§ 4). A **`geometry_hash`** difference is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` when the instance carries history, meaning any non-`FREE` socket, any `welds[]` row naming it, or a body shared with another section, because a moved socket or wall edge under a welded or cut instance restores with broken abutment; on a never-welded `FREE` instance alone it is accepted with the diagnostic `geometry_changed_fresh`, the rects are re-derived from the new template and the stored hash is rewritten. A **`visual_hash`** difference alone is accepted with `visual_changed` and rewritten. A hash collision cannot hide a structural change that also changes a tile set or key sequence in a way the validation of step (6) detects; a 2^-32 collision on `structure_hash` is accepted and recorded (§ Risks R6). Pre-release saves are disposable; after the first outside build the migration obligation of LY-6 e applies, and a rewritten hash means the next snapshot differs from the stored one, so the K-4 `state_hash` compare reports a mismatch as a diagnostic, as designed.
321	
322	**Query validity after restore.** Class 1 (static, valid when `restore()` returns): `room_at`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `room_surface`, `socket_plan`, `anchor_geometry`, static rect membership, `section_offset`, `body_of`, `section_at`. Class 2 (leaf-dependent, valid after `post_restore()`): `rects_in`/`solid_in` door leaves, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `door_passage_into`. Between the two they report the template default (every leaf closed) and raise `stale_leaf` if read; `LayoutDerived.leaves_valid` is the flag. The kernel guarantees every `restore()` completes before any `post_restore()` begins.
323	
324	**`post_restore(ctx)`** (a) runs one `derive_doors` pass over the leaf cache using `opening_into` (an `area` above `area_max` is clamped with a diagnostic, and the same fault found *here* is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING`; an unknown opening leaves the leaf closed); (b) rebuilds `opening_leaves` from the restored `welds[]` and `seam_openings_into`; (c) bumps `version` and `leaf_version` (never `static_version`) for each section whose derived leaf set differs from the all-closed default, so a restored open door is a 1 to 2 transition and every rebuilding consumer rebuilds on tick 1 with no ordering between `post_restore` calls; (d) runs cross-block **verification** through `section_counts_into`: every `graph_ref_base` resolves (node, edge and compartment counts match the template), every `welds[]` `seam_id` resolves to a Graph seam record, and `graph.next_section_id == layout.next_section_id`. Failures use the restore codes. Verification order and the "installed `def_id` at a hardpoint resolves" diagnostic belong to ADR-0016's verifier list; this ADR supplies the checks Layout's side can run. After a restore every section reports `changed_region` ALL once, and the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch (ADR-0003 § 4).
325	
326	**Policy line (TR-derelict-008 Layout half).** A save restores from its **saved values**: templates are never mutated at runtime, a restore never re-templates an instance, and no Authoring content lint runs at restore.

330	Reads are pure, side-effect free, deterministic and identical before a snapshot and after restoring it (idempotent), and have **no "perceived" variant** (Pillar 1, TR-section-039). Cold reads that depend only on a template (`room_adjacency`, `south_band`, `plate_positions`) are precomputed once per template in the catalog row, so a read is a copy, not a recomputation.

347	### 13. Scene boundary and the PROJECTOR's inputs
348	
349	The Layout data module references no `Node`, `Node2D`, `TileMapLayer`, `SceneTree`, `Resource` subclass or engine physics type (AC-120); a headless run leaves the orphan-node count unchanged. The PROJECTOR (`src/presentation/projector/`, ADR-0034) is a separate subscriber that never writes a block and never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D`, builds door, prop, machinery and bead/plate/scar sprites from the rect table and `welds[]`/socket state, and redraws on `SEC`, `BODY`, `SEAM` and `LEAF` keys. This ADR guarantees the three inputs of the sprite `entity_id` are stable: `section_id` (never reused, below 2^20), a closed `kind_ordinal` vocabulary (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar), and `template_local_idx` (the rect `idx` or the template placement index, below the rect stride and so below 2^16). The packing function and the namespace byte `LAYOUT_ID_NS` belong to ADR-0034 and the Pipeline (OQ-33); Layout exports no packing helper and tiles carry no `entity_id`.

413	### Implementation Guidelines
414	
415	- **Must** register exactly one block (`layout.state`), one hook (`layout.doors`), one fault domain (4), one key space `{SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3, LEAF 4}` and one diagnostics channel, only through `ModuleFacet.registrar` in `BOOTING`; **must never** register a second Layout block or a `layout.templates` block.
416	- **Must** store instances by reference (`template_id` plus drift hashes plus runtime fields); **must never** put geometry, a rect, a leaf, a tile list, a `kind`, a `visited` bit, a loose-item row, a door `area` or `door_state`, a float, a `layout_hash` or `mutation_count` in `layout.state`.
417	- **Must** snapshot as the § 2 closed key set of parallel columns, ascending ids, duplicated packed arrays; **must never** use an int-keyed `Dictionary`, `PackedStringArray`, `Vector2i`, `Rect2i`, `StringName` or `Resource` in the payload, and **must never** put a key in the payload that is not on the regenerated allow-list.
418	- **Must** keep `section_id == row + 1` and `body_id == row + 1`: an id is consumed only by the call that appends its row; **must never** reuse, renumber, skip or reserve an id, and **must never** let a counter wrap (the `can_*` check fails first).
419	- **Must** pass the Graph the section id and store the returned `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`; **must never** allocate a node, edge, compartment or seam id in Layout, and **must never** read the Graph's `next_*` counters except in the post-restore verification.
420	- **Must** compare stored hashes as `value & 0xFFFFFFFF` (`IntMath.low32`); **must never** compare a `PackedInt32Array`-read hash unmasked.
421	- **Must** compute the three template hashes once at catalog freeze with `Hash64.of_value` over the § 4 sub-payloads; **must never** write owner byte encoders for them (ADR-0005 `owner_canonical_byte_writer`) and **must never** store them in a template file.
422	- **Must** write a socket's state only inside LM2 and LM3 and choose the weld survivor by lower `body_id`; **must never** add a `set_socket_state` or `install_cap_plate` mutator, and **must never** let the result of a weld depend on argument order.
423	- **Must** begin every mutator with `scope.open_for(&"layout.state")`, check every Class A status, mark keys explicitly (`DirtyKey.make`) after the writes; **must never** rely on a packed-array property setter for dirty tracking (4.7), and **must never** call a Graph mutator from a `can_*` check.
424	- **Must** make LM2 seed each new LEAF closed with its last-projected cache and **must never** read the Graph's `area` inside LM2; **must** make `layout.doors` bump a section's `leaf_version` at most once per tick and **never** `static_version`.
425	- **Must** treat every door `area` write as a P2 write by command; **must never** call `set_opening_area` from a hook, and **must never** store, mirror or write `area` or `door_state` in Layout.
426	- **Must** use `IntMath.floor_div` for every px-to-cell, px-to-tile and leaf computation and avoid `/`, `%`, `/=`, `%=` in `src/sim/layout/`; **must never** use `float`, `Vector2`, `Rect2` or any engine geometry type in the module.
427	- **Must** take foot boxes as caller arguments; **must never** read `body.state` from Layout (acyclic restore, `restore_after: []`).
428	- **Must** make `restore` validate into scratch and copy into the existing `LayoutState`; **must never** replace the object a facade wraps, alias `data`, or return a partial restore; **must** reject `rot_q != 0` and any `structure_hash` mismatch.
429	- **Must** tag the hot reads of § 11 `## @hot`; **must never** allocate in `room_at`, `section_at`, `body_of`, `door_passage_into`, `leaf_would_overlap` or the hook (ADR-0010 `HOT-01`, flat `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` over N ticks).
430	- **Must** keep `src/sim/layout/` scene-tree free and `src/data/` free of `src/sim/` imports; the PROJECTOR script **must never** live under `src/sim/layout/`.
431	- **Must** enforce capacity ceilings in `can_build`/`can_detach` before any id is consumed or the Graph is called.
432	- **Must** load every Layout knob from `LayoutTuning`; **must never** put a literal for a knob in module source.

434	## Alternatives Considered
435	
436	### Alternative 1: Full geometry in the block
437	- **Description**: Each instance stores its rooms, rect table, sockets and doors in `layout.state`.
438	- **Pros**: A save is self-contained; a template edit cannot affect an old save; no catalog dependency at restore.
439	- **Cons**: Rectangles times sections times snapshot cadence bloat the block (hundreds of rects per ship against tens of rows); authored data is duplicated into every save; the Vertical Slice "seed plus deltas" model is defeated; an exporter bug is persisted forever; the hash covers authored data that is already hashed at catalog freeze.
440	- **Rejection Reason**: Instances by reference with drift hashes keeps the block at tens of KB, and the drift policy already turns a template edit into a loud restore failure where it matters.
441	
442	### Alternative 2: A second block `layout.templates`
443	- **Description**: Templates become a persisted block of their own so the save carries what it was built from.
444	- **Pros**: Restore never consults the catalog.
445	- **Cons**: A second restore root and a second hash for data that never changes at runtime; it contradicts ADR-0007's "catalogs are not state blocks"; it duplicates the content pipeline's integrity checks.
446	- **Rejection Reason**: Static data belongs to the catalog; the block stores references.
447	
448	### Alternative 3: Array-of-`Dictionary` or int-keyed `Dictionary` tables in the snapshot
449	- **Description**: One row per instance as a `Dictionary`, or a table keyed by id.
450	- **Pros**: Readable dumps; trivial lookup by id.
451	- **Cons**: JSON turns int keys into strings and numbers into floats (LY-26 a); a per-row `Dictionary` allocates and sorts per row in the encoder; ADR-0005 § 3.6 asks blocks with more than about 250 scalar fields to use packed arrays; two equal worlds reached by different histories could order differently.
452	- **Rejection Reason**: Dense parallel columns in ascending id order are the shape ADR-0005 and ADR-0006 are built for, and `id - 1` row addressing removes the lookup map.
453	
454	### Alternative 4: The Graph allocates `section_id` (and Layout asks for it)
455	- **Description**: `build_section` calls M1 first and takes the section id from the return.
456	- **Pros**: One fewer counter in Layout.
457	- **Cons**: Layout cannot name its own row, dirty key or body before the Graph runs; the `rect_key` bound (2^20) becomes the Graph's responsibility; Layout's `can_build` could not test the section-id ceiling before calling the Graph; two persisted counters would both claim to be the section counter.
458	- **Rejection Reason**: The GDD and the Graph (LS-15) already treat the section id as a caller input to M1. Layout allocates; the Graph's counter follows.
459	
460	### Alternative 5: Layout also allocates the Graph's node, edge and compartment ids
461	- **Description**: Layout hands the Graph explicit id ranges.
462	- **Pros**: `graph_ref_base` becomes Layout's alone.
463	- **Cons**: Layout would have to know the Graph's per-template node and edge counts and its capacity rules; two owners could both write the Graph's counters.
464	- **Rejection Reason**: One writer per fact; the Graph returns the bases it allocated.
465	
466	### Alternative 6: A nested ledger (one entry per template with a `room_keys` list), or two ledger spaces
467	- **Description**: `pairs[]` holds templates, each with a nested list of room keys; or `section_templates` and `section_rooms` are separate spaces.
468	- **Pros**: Mirrors the data's shape.
469	- **Cons**: A nested form needs a second `verify` and a second append-only gate (the generic one compares pairs); a per-template list makes "remove one room" a list edit instead of a per-pair `dormant` flip; two spaces mean two files and a cross-file foreign-key check.
470	- **Rejection Reason**: One flat space with compound keys reuses ADR-0007 unchanged and keeps the CI diff a list of added pairs.
471	
472	### Alternative 7: Owner-written TLV for the template hashes (ADR-LAY-06 as the GDD wrote it)
473	- **Description**: `canonical_geometry_bytes` as `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` in a documented field order.
474	- **Pros**: Independent of the kernel encoder.
475	- **Cons**: ADR-0005 § 3.1 forbids owner byte writers and ships golden vectors for the kernel's TLV only; a second encoder is a second injectivity argument.
476	- **Rejection Reason**: ADR-LAY-06 becomes the payload shape; the byte form is ADR-0005's.
477	
478	### Alternative 8: Two hashes only, with sets compared at restore
479	- **Description**: Keep the GDD's `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash`; classify "structural" by comparing key sets.
480	- **Pros**: The row stays 13 fields.
481	- **Cons**: There is nothing persisted to compare key sets against; a pure reorder passes every count and set and silently re-points ids to the wrong rooms and sockets.
482	- **Rejection Reason**: § 4. The third hash costs four bytes a row and makes the check exact.
483	
484	### Alternative 9: Weld survivor by argument order, or by larger body
485	- **Description**: The first argument's body survives; or the body with more sections.
486	- **Pros**: Simple call site.
487	- **Cons**: Caller mixups can dissolve the home ship and make two equal worlds hash differently; the larger-body rule changes with every weld.
488	- **Rejection Reason**: The lower `body_id` is persisted, immutable and total.
489	
490	### Alternative 10: Derive leaves lazily on read (the GDD fallback)
491	- **Description**: No hook; a leaf is derived when a query asks, stamped by the Graph's write state.
492	- **Pros**: No P3 cost.
493	- **Cons**: A read mutates a derived cache; a refresh in P2 can precede a later same-P2 change to `area`; every consumer pays the check.
494	- **Rejection Reason**: The hook is ordered (`body.integrate after layout.doors`) and bounded; the fallback stays recorded but unused.
495	
496	### Alternative 11: Persist all sockets densely (including `FREE`)
497	- **Description**: A row per declared socket per instance.
498	- **Pros**: Fixed-size table; no sorted insert.
499	- **Cons**: Most rows are `FREE` forever in MVP; a template that adds a socket changes the table shape (a structural change even for an unwelded instance).
500	- **Rejection Reason**: Sparse non-`FREE` rows are smaller and a template that adds a socket does not touch old saves except through the structure hash, which is already exact.
501	
502	## Consequences
503	
504	### Positive
505	- One block, one owner, one closed payload shape that the type walk, the encoder and the allow-list test all agree on.
506	- Row addressing by `id - 1` removes id maps from every hot read and makes the dense-id check a restore invariant.
507	- A weld or cut gives the same bytes for the same world regardless of argument order, so `state_hash` equality and replay hold.
508	- The structural check is exact (a reorder is refused), where the GDD's wording would have corrupted old saves.
509	- Capacity ceilings fail in validate with a named reason, never as a `FAULTED` apply, and no counter can wrap.
510	- The Layout/Graph id boundary is a table; each side can be tested with the other stubbed through `LayoutGraphPort`.
511	- ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016 and ADR-0034 build on records and rules that no longer move.
512	
513	### Negative
514	- The instance row grows to 14 columns, deviating from the TR text; the GDD, TR-section-004, D.21 and the AC-130 allow-list are updated.
515	- Dense ids forbid reserving an id; a future procgen that wants sparse or hashed ids must supersede this ADR.
516	- `layout.doors` marks a key and therefore advances `touch_serial` on door-change ticks, invalidating the block hash cache on those ticks.
517	- A new key family (LEAF) is added to a key space the GDD listed as closed.
518	- A template reorder now refuses every old save of that template (correctly, but harshly); authors must append rooms, not reorder them, once the first build is outside the project.
519	- Layout depends on a port whose Graph-side implementation does not exist yet.
520	
521	## Risks
522	- **R1: dense-id invariant broken by a future feature.** A mutator that consumes an id without a row breaks `id == row + 1`. Mitigation: restore asserts it; a unit test builds, discards and restores and checks it; a lint `LAY-ID-01` forbids writes to the counters outside LM1 and LM3.
523	- **R2: the third hash is a deviation.** A reviewer may prefer the GDD's two. Mitigation: the reasoning is in § 4 with the failing scenario; reverting is a one-column change before any save exists.
524	- **R3: hook-marked keys and hash cache churn.** If animating doors become continuous (a stepped slide, OQ-14 c), a key per tick advances `touch_serial` every tick. Mitigation: binary doors in MVP; the cost is bounded by block size; revisit with ADR-0005 § 5.4 if continuous doors are introduced.
525	- **R4: GDScript cost of the hook and of attach/detach.** All figures are pending-spike (V2, V3). Mitigation: the fallback ladder of ADR-0010 § 9; hook early-out on a Graph change counter; attach/detach are rare P2 events.
526	- **R5: element writes without a setter (4.7).** A missed dirty mark is a stale display. Mitigation: explicit marks inside mutators, the ADR-0004 audit (`quiet_writes_allowed` false), and a per-mutator key fixture.
527	- **R6: hash collisions.** `low32` of a 64-bit hash collides at 2^-32 per pair. Mitigation: hashes are diagnostic gates, restore step (6) re-validates structure against the current template independently, and a missed geometry change on an instance with history would at worst restore with a wrong abutment that the weld-offset check of step (6) catches.
528	- **R7: the Graph port is unwritten.** If ADR-0011 returns non-contiguous ranges or an allocating `opening` read, §§ 3, 8 and 10 change. Mitigation: § Related lists the exact assumptions; ADR-0011 and this ADR are reviewed together.
529	- **R8: attach can exceed the per-body rect ceiling.** `can_attach` has no `BODY_FULL` reason. Mitigation: the MVP world is a few hundred rects against `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`; a world lint bounds the sum; OQ-1.
530	- **R9: `Array[String]` column in the type walk.** Mitigation: V5; the fallback is a ledger-integer column with the string recovered from the catalog, which is a schema-version bump.
531	- **R10: template edits after the first outside build.** Authors can break old saves. Mitigation: the ledger flips to `SHIPPED` at the same moment; CI append-only gates; the drift policy is loud, not silent.

587	## Performance Implications
588	- **CPU**: `layout.doors` <= 0.2 ms at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` on a release export (V2). Reads on the hot tier are index arithmetic and one `bsearch` at most; none allocates. LM1 to LM4 and restore are cold P2 or boundary events with a per-body grid rebuild (V3, ADR-0014); `can_attach` uncached <= 2 ms, memoised. `layout_hash()` is never per tick.

Catalog templates hold the compiled rect table once per template.
590	- **Load Time**: three `Hash64.of_value` passes per template at catalog freeze (four templates in MVP), once. Restore validates and rebuilds in one cold pass.
591	- **Network**: none in MVP; `SHARED_SUMMARY` replication is the instance table plus three hashes (VS-B, ADR-0032).
592	
593	## Migration Plan
594	There is no Layout code yet, so nothing migrates. Story order for the epic: (1) `TemplateCompiler` and the three hashes in `SectionTemplates`, with the ledger check; (2) `LayoutState`, `snapshot`/`restore`/`default_state` and the allow-list test; (3) LM1 with the `LayoutGraphPort` stub; (4) `layout.doors` and the leaf queries; (5) LM2/LM3 with the weld property tests (ADR-0021 shares them); (6) LM4 and the read views; (7) `post_restore` and verification (with ADR-0016). **GDD sync** (listed in the result and applied by the orchestrator): TR-section-004 and AC-130 to the 14-column payload and key names; LY-6 e and LY-26 e from sets to ordered sequences and the third hash; D.10, OQ-10 and the ADR-LAY-06 notes from owner TLV to payload shape; LY-32 and the key-space table to add LEAF; LY-14, LY-16, LY-17 and LY-27 for `out` records and `preview_attach`; D.21 for 14 columns; LY-26 a for native int64 times; LY-4 for the ledger nesting.
595	
596	## Validation Criteria
597	- The AC-130 allow-list test (regenerated) walks the MVP snapshot and finds exactly the § 2 keys.
598	- Round trip: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical; equal worlds built by different histories (build, weld, cut versus restore) hash equal; `mutation_count` appears in no payload (AC-172).
599	- Weld symmetry: `attach_section(a, b)` and `attach_section(b, a)` produce a byte-identical block and equal `AttachResult`; the lower `body_id` always survives.
600	- Detach: `detach_preview(seam)` equals LM3's `moved_sections`, `frame_shift_px` and `rects`; exactly two components; the property test over generated section pairs (ADR-0021) holds.
601	- Dense ids: build, discard and restore keep `section_id == row + 1`; a hand-edited non-dense payload fails `LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`; the section ceiling returns `CAPACITY` before any id is consumed, and counters at `2^31 - 1` never wrap.
602	- Drift: a room reorder fails `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` on a fresh instance; a wall-edge edit fails on a welded instance and succeeds with `geometry_changed_fresh` on a fresh one; a visual-only edit succeeds with `visual_changed`; `rot_q = 1` fails `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`; a hash at or above 2^31 compares equal after the mask.
603	- Leaves: a closed leaf blocks and an open one does not in the tick its state changes (P2 write, P3 read); LM2 leaves the span solid with no `stale_leaf` and no `leaf_version` bump at the first P3; an unknown opening leaves the leaf closed with one `opening_unknown`; `area > area_max` clamps with a diagnostic; at most one bump per section per tick; `static_version` never bumps from the hook; the hook's cost line (V2).
604	- Dirty keys: the per-mutator fixture asserts the specific keys (LM2 5, LM3 6 in D.12's example, `LEAF` from the hook) and the ADR-0004 audit raises no `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK`.
605	- Static scans: no `Node`/`Resource`/float/`/` in `src/sim/layout/`; no write to `sockets` columns or counters outside the named mutators; no unmasked hash compare.
606	- S4 loaded-set test through real `build_section` calls: tile and rect totals within the ceilings.
607	- Golden vectors for the three template hashes of the four MVP templates, equal on editor and export (V4).

134:- `GraphView.step_no()` is `IntMath.floor_div(clock.tick(), tuning.graph_step_ticks)`, a pure function of `T` available at any call site (Failure & Trail compares it with its poll cache, FT-15; the Item DB's `validate_instance` compares against it, TR-itemdb-014). `hdr.last_step_no` is the last step whose power hook completed and is persisted for restore; the two differ only between a tick and its first hook.
175:**The overlay is normative**: each kind-specific reading of `stock`, `req`, `req_max`, `aux_a`, `aux_b`, `tier`, `subtype` is exposed only through a named accessor on `GraphView` or a writer (`reactor_fuel_rem(slot)`, `reservoir_t_cool(slot)`, `hull_bound_compartment(slot)`), never by raw column index outside the writer and snapshot files. The alternative (a side table per kind) costs an extra row-index map per table for the sake of a few bytes per row on about 105 nodes (Alternative 5).
183:**3.6 `seams` columns:** `id`, `section_a`, `section_b`, `q`, `hp` (the seam's weld quality x 10), `leak_bp`, `l_seam`, `built_step`, `mode_since` (i32); `mode_key`, `state` (ACTIVE, CUT), `boundary` (SEALED, RAGGED; 0 while ACTIVE) (u8); and three CSR pairs into flat lists `edge_ids`, `opening_ids`, `stub_ids` (`edge_first`/`edge_count`, `open_first`/`open_count`, `stub_first`/`stub_count`, all i32). A SeamRecord is never deleted: a cut turns it into a tombstone with state CUT, its lists intact (the cut-hole ids `seam_view` reports). **The hull stubs of a RAGGED cut are ordinary HULL_SEGMENT node rows appended at the cut** (flags STUB, `hp` 2500 as LS-16, `aux_a` the bound compartment), listed in `stub_ids`; the GDD's "hull-stub records ... no new persisted field" is therefore satisfied by existing columns, and `cut_detach` can append rows, so `can_detach` must include `CAPACITY`, as the Layout GDD already lists it (`can_detach` reasons, amended 2026-10-27; ADR-0012/0021 implement it).
253:**6.2 Aliasing and the Jacobi pair.** S0-a, the packed-array aliasing question the GDD left open, is **closed for the data model by ADR-0005 P7 and probes (c), (d)**: a `Packed*Array` is shared by reference by assignment, by argument and by a getter, an element write through any alias is visible through all, and only `duplicate()` isolates (by deferred copy-on-write, probe (e)). Consequences, as rules: **(1)** a function may take a local alias of a column for reads and writes within one phase (no one resizes during a phase); **(2)** an alias is never kept across a kernel call, a `snapshot`, a `restore` or a structural mutator (`resize` and member re-assignment would orphan it); **(3)** a snapshot is never a local alias: it is a `duplicate()` placed in the payload (ADR-0003); **(4)** Jacobi's "start-of-phase snapshot" is two member arrays, the `GraphState` column and a `GraphScratch` `next` array of the same length, swapped by reference at the phase end (`var t: PackedInt64Array = state_col; state_col = scratch_next; scratch_next = t`, allocation-free, probe (c)). Which columns are double-buffered and when the swap happens is ADR-0012's; the data model's contribution is that `next` arrays live in `GraphScratch`, are sized with the table, and that anything holding a column reference reads it through the member each time (the `GraphView` facade reads `state` members, never a cached array), so a swap cannot strand a reader.
325:**8.3 Numeric soft violations.** A value above its column maximum or below zero where it cannot be, a conservation drift or a clamped `dT` (LS-24): in release the writer clamps, increments `GraphDiag.saturations[field]` and continues; with `strict_numeric` (injected into `GraphModule.setup()` by the composition root: true in tests and `STRICT_DEBUG`) it raises `GraphFaults.SATURATION` instead. Every Graph test suite asserts `saturations` is all zeros. The two builds differ only after a defect, so the build-mode equivalence of ADR-0003 holds on a clean stream. A legal clamp (the stock reconcile, § 7.3) is not a saturation.
331:**9.1 `GraphView`.** `read_view(ctx)` is called once at the registry freeze and puts one long-lived `GraphView` (`src/sim/graph/views/graph_view.gd`, getter-only) that holds references to the single `GraphState`, `GraphCaches`, the frozen `GraphTuning` and the read-only `ClockView`; `empty_view(ctx)` puts a `GraphView` built over an empty state whose getters return neutral values (`is_empty()` true). The view reads members each call (§ 6.2). It is **pure**: no getter writes any member of any of the four classes, emits no dirty key and draws no RNG; it may call `ensure_derived()`, which is a no-op guard because every structural mutator and `post_restore` already finished by rebuilding (LS-19, and this keeps `validate`'s hash-unchanged guarantee). adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md:92:        |                                            section_rects_into(section_id, mask, out)
adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md:102:**One structure, three consumers' views.** For every LIVE body `RectIndex` owns one `BodyGrid`. Its core is a **row table** with one row per rect slot of every section on the body: every static rect, every door-leaf slot and every socket PLATE/JAMB slot of ADR-0013 § 5, **including slots that are currently inactive or zero-length** (they keep their row, exactly as they keep their `idx`). `rects_in` and `solid_in` are not two indexes: they are **two flag masks over this one table** (`OCCLUDES_LIGHT` and `SOLID`, registry `layout_rect_flags`). A third reader, the PROJECTOR, reads the same rows through `section_rects_into` (§ 5). That single table is what TR-section-011 means by "one rect set": no consumer has a private copy to drift, and no query has a perceived or phantom variant.

209:**Bump API (Layout-internal; nothing else writes these columns).** `bump_static(section_id)` adds 1 to `static_version` and to `version`; `bump_leaf(section_id)` adds 1 to `leaf_version` and to `version`; `invalidate(section_id)` sets all three to 0 (discard). The closed list of callers is ADR-0013 § 7/§ 8/§ 10 and the GDD's LY-12 d: `build_section` (0 to 1), `attach_section` and `detach_section` (`bump_static` on **every section whose socket state changes, including the host that does not move, and every moved section**), `discard_section_geometry` (**`invalidate`**: a cached consumer sees a change to 0, and since ids are never reused 0 cannot alias a later section; **this is an explicit deviation: it replaces the "bump on discard" of Layout GDD LY-12 d and ADR-0013 § 7/§ 10 with a value no live section can hold** (a GDD sync item and a cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0013 carry it), and it makes `version()` agree with ADR-0013 § 11's "0 for an unknown or discarded section"), `layout.doors` (`bump_leaf`, at most once per section per tick, never `static_version`) and `post_restore` (`bump_leaf` for each section whose derived leaf set is not all-closed, so a restored open door is a 1 to 2 transition). A weld of two single-section bodies therefore bumps both sections' `static_version`; a door animating bumps `leaf_version` and `version` only (AC-182's matrix is the test).
211:**`version_epoch` (additive).** The GDD resets all counters to 1 on `restore` and then tells consumers to remember to rebuild unconditionally, "because a post-restore `version` can numerically equal a pre-restore cached value". That is a convention a future consumer can forget. `LayoutVersions.version_epoch` is an `int`, 1 at boot, **incremented by every whole-block replacement** (`restore` and `default_state`, the two calls that reset the counters), never persisted, never hashed, never read by a block. A consumer caches `(version_epoch, version)`; an epoch change is "rebuild everything" by definition, with no ordering assumption between `post_restore` calls. Consumers may *also* use the kernel's restore signals (`PresentationClock.load_seq`, the `ALL` batch, the Emitter's own `post_restore`); the epoch makes the port self-sufficient. The name is chosen so it is not confused with `restore_epoch` (ADR-0003/ADR-0005, the RNG epoch), which this ADR does not read.
213:**`changed_region` (simulation-side, current tick only).** Per section: `kind` (`ChangedRegion.NONE 0, ALL 1, REGION 2, FRAME 3`), a `REGION` box (four `int32`, body frame) and a `stamp_tick`. The writers are the same mutators as the bumps, through `stamp_all`, `stamp_region(box)` and `stamp_frame`. **Validity is lazy, not cleared:** a read returns NONE unless `stamp_tick == ClockView.tick()`. `T` advances only in the tick driver's boundary (ADR-0003 § 10), so a stamp written in P2 of tick `T` is read by `emitter.place` in P3 of the same `T`, and goes silent at `T + 1` with no clearing pass. **Merge lattice when one section is stamped twice in a tick** (a socket-host section in LM2 in P2, then its leaf in the P3 hook): `ALL` absorbs everything; `REGION` with `REGION` is the bounding union; `FRAME` with `REGION` is `REGION` (the reader detects a translation by comparing `section_offset`, as the GDD says); `FRAME` with `FRAME` is `FRAME`. The values are the GDD's (build, discard, `post_restore` = ALL; a leaf change = REGION(union of old and new leaf rects); a socket-host section = REGION(union of that socket's PLATE, JAMB and LEAF slot footprints); every other moved section = FRAME). **Presentation must not read it**: a rendered frame can follow up to four ticks, so "this tick" is meaningless there; presentation uses the dirty batch and `version`. After a restore, "every section reports ALL once" holds only if the first step after `post_restore` observes the same `T` that `post_restore` stamped; that is not guaranteed by anything this ADR can see, so **the authoritative restore signal is `version_epoch`** and a consumer must not rely on `changed_region == ALL` after a restore (§ Open Questions 1).

181:- A restore is idempotent: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical except for the closed `REBASE_BLOCKS` list (SL-12), and the Graph's, Body's and Controller's tests prove it.
187:**2.5 `hash_algo` and `codec`.** `hash_algo` 2 names H64 (the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, read little-endian, ratified by the GDD, owned by ADR-0005); 0 and 1 are reserved, never written (they are `hash_algo` ids, not hash values: no `H64` value is reserved as a sentinel, ADR-0005). An unsupported `hash_algo` skips the reproduction compare (`SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`, REBASED cause 4) so a kernel hash change is never a save-breaking event. `codec` 0 only.
193:**3.1 Ownership and storage.** Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`, an unsigned 32-bit integer (an `int` in `[0, 2^32 - 1]`) starting at 0 at `new_game` (SL-18); it has exactly one owner and registry entry. It lives in a per-slot **pair of side files**, `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch_a.bin` and `slot_epoch_b.bin`, each **12 bytes: the epoch as `u32` LE, a sequence number `seq` as `u32` LE, then the CRC32 of those 8 bytes as `u32` LE** (the GDD / TR-saveload-020 format of `u32` plus CRC32 gains the `seq` field; GDD sync). The reader takes the valid file (size 12, CRC matches) with the higher `seq`; the writer always overwrites the **older** file in place (an invalid file, or the lower `seq`) with `seq = max + 1`, flushes, closes, re-reads and checks the CRC (that re-read is the `EPOCH_DURABLE` report). **No rename and no remove is involved**, so there is never an instant with no valid epoch file: a kill mid-write corrupts only the file being written and the other still holds the previous durable value. (A single file replaced by rename-over would, on Windows, probably be remove-then-rename, § 1.5, open a window in which the file is absent, and let the rebuild rule of § 3.4 yield `max(header copy) + 1`, which can be lower than an epoch already advanced, for example after two deaths with no autosave between them, replaying one set of threat draws; engine review E2.) `seq` saturates at 2^32 - 1, unreachable in practice because the epoch saturates first. `SlotEpoch.encode` calls `resize(12)` before any `encode_u32` (probe 17). **CRC32 is hand-rolled** (polynomial `0xEDB88320`, init and final XOR `0xFFFFFFFF`, bitwise, over 8 bytes): `PackedByteArray` has no `crc32` (probed), the scripted loop matched the standard check vector, its cost is of order microseconds, and a truncated hash was rejected as a gratuitous change to the GDD format. The vector `crc32("123456789") == 0xCBF43926` is a unit test. The files are in no generation, so no generation's bytes, trailer, `state_hash` or any key derived from them changes after `VERIFYING`; this is what makes SL-12's REBASED baseline key stable (R14). Each WORLD generation's header carries a **read-only write-time copy** (`restore_epoch`, an int below 2^32) used only by the rebuild rule of § 3.4; it is never rewritten.
373:- **Cons**: Rewriting a verified file changes its trailer and every key derived from it (SL-12's REBASED baseline), races the write protocol, and loses the value when that generation is quarantined or the ring steps back.

content.content:
The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.

| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
|---|---|---|
| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |

`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.

225:**SL-12 — Verification: file stage, reproduction stage, and the verification window.** Verification has two stages (Formula `save_verification`, Formulas). The **file stage** is always on and runs before the kernel is touched: trailer SHA-256, every `payload_sha256`, structure. The **reproduction stage** proves the restore reproduced the snapshot: after the last `post_restore()` and **before the first `RUNNING` tick**, recompute `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` (D.12, cited, never restated) over the restored WORLD blocks and compare it with the header's `state_hash`. **Validity guard (needs no kernel hook):** the compare counts only if `kernel.clock.T` equals the header `T` at compare time; otherwise `SL_VERIFY_WINDOW_MISSED` is logged and **no verdict is recorded** (a hash taken after a tick has run would differ for the wrong reason). Its mode is **EXACT** unless one of five closed **REBASED causes** holds: (1) a migration ran, (2) a retired block was stripped, (3) `default_state()` filled a missing block, (4) the header's `hash_algo` is unsupported by this build (the compare is skipped with `SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`; the state hash is a bug detector, and refusing on it would make a kernel hash change a save-breaking event, contradicting SL-16), or (5) a member of the Save/Load-owned build constant `REBASE_BLOCKS` is present in the file. In REBASED mode *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the baseline is now read back — the next restore of the same generation, with the same key (`generation`, `build_id`, `registry_epoch`, `trailer_sha8`), `trailer_sha8` being the first 8 lowercase hex characters of the trailer SHA-256 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: a byte-different file with the same generation number is a different baseline)*; the key is stable because no generation file is rewritten after `VERIFYING`: `restore_epoch` lives in the per-slot `slot_epoch` side-file pair (SL-23, delegated ruling R14), so a restore changes neither a generation's bytes nor its trailer, and the second restore of a generation always finds its baseline (`BASELINE_MATCH` or `BASELINE_DIVERGED` are reachable) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*; compares its recomputed value with the baseline recorded last time and reports `BASELINE_MATCH` or `BASELINE_DIVERGED` (F-4), so a REBASED load is no longer vacuous against a non-deterministic restore; a first restore records, a later one checks, and a manifest rebuilt from headers has no baseline and re-records)* the recomputed value is recorded as the generation's baseline **in `campaign.json` only** (a hint — SL-14 forbids writing back to the file) and `SL_VERIFY_REBASED{cause}` is logged; it is not a failure. In EXACT mode a mismatch is `SL_VERIFY_NOT_REPRODUCED{blocks}` (naming the diverging blocks when the kernel exposes per-block hashes): **release** builds mark the generation `suspect` in `campaign.json` and **play on**; **dev and test** builds halt on the first occurrence (it is a K:839 / G4 regression). A reproduction mismatch **never falls back to another generation**: the file stage has already proved the bytes, so a mismatch after a successful restore is deterministic code (`restore(snapshot) ≠ identity`) that reproduces on every generation, and walking the ring would strand the player on an intact ring with `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE` for our own defect. `SUSPECT_THRESHOLD` is a diagnostics escalation only. *(Orchestrator ruling — findings the first rulings did not settle, as amended at the stage-5 checkpoint. (1) R10 says the compare runs after every restore in every build; applied literally, the first schema bump would fail every older generation (a migrated block's canonical bytes differ from the stored ones), hence the EXACT/REBASED modes and their closed cause set. (2) **Restore-idempotence is the kernel's rule, not a Save/Load request:** K:839 already requires, for every registered block, that the snapshot → interchange → restore → snapshot round trip yields byte-identical canonical bytes, and G:1096 is the Graph's instance of it; a registration flag that let a block opt out would be a CR-8 field invented by Save/Load and would make verification permanently vacuous, so none exists. The Controller's restore is a non-identity (PC-17: `octant`, `run` and `channel_ref` reset and `CHANNELLING` / `STAGGERED` become `IDLE`; the Controller draft's Body text zeroed `sub` and set `previous := current` in `post_restore`, P:913, while P:285 persists `sub` — answered for `body.state` by Ship Body & Interior Physics BDY-31: `post_restore` preserves `sub`, and `body.state` is restore-idempotent at block level *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*), and the Controller's G4 claim (P:1045) cannot hold while the control run carries sub-pixel residue that the restored run zeroes and the live Adapter's resync command is absent from a replayed stream. That is routed to the Controller/Body author as a **CONFLICT against K:839 and G4** naming those three specifics — PC-17 restore normalisation; `sub = 0` and `previous := current` in `post_restore` against a persisted `sub`; the P:1045 replay claim against the residue and the absent resync command (OQ-9) — and the resolution is the owners': express the normalisation in `snapshot()` or move it out of restore. **Interim, Save/Load-owned and provisional** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: one reading of PC-17 across this rule, SL-15 item 10, OQ-9, OQ-39 and the knob row)*: the build constant `REBASE_BLOCKS` lists the blocks whose presence selects REBASED mode. **Default `[interaction.state, assembly.state]`.** `controller.state` and `body.state` are **not** listed: the Controller answered that PC-17 normalises in `snapshot()` and that `restore()` is a whole-block replace, and BDY-31 makes `body.state` restore-idempotent at block level, so the automated AC-SL-67 (a mid-move `controller.state` fixture compared in EXACT mode) is the gate that proves it, and a story whose fixture fails it re-adds the block with a dated debt entry. `interaction.state` and `assembly.state` still clear transient fields in `post_restore` (IA-36, MSA-4), so a generation saved mid-channel or inside Assembly's pending window would verify `NOT_REPRODUCED` and halt a dev build on a routine quit mid-weld; they are listed **now**, so no merge halts dev builds, and the **exit** is that the owners move the clears into `snapshot()` (OQ-39, routed), after which Save/Load empties the list and the default becomes `[]`. A non-empty list is a known kernel-contract debt: while it holds, every real MVP file contains a listed block and verifies REBASED, which makes the reproduction stage diagnostic-only for real saves (the recorded baseline above still catches a restore that is not deterministic), and a CI check fails the first outside build while the list is non-empty (SL-14). The through-disk G4 criteria run on the kernel's stand-in blocks, `graph.state`, `controller.state` and `body.state`, and AC-SL-67 is a merge gate for the Controller, Interaction and Assembly stories. (3) **K-4 (adopted by the kernel, CR-15)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash: int = 0, has_expected_hash: bool = false)` *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*. When `has_expected_hash` is true the kernel recomputes `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` after the last `post_restore()`, inside `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, and reports `{T, computed_hash, verdict}` (verdict `MATCH` / `MISMATCH` / `NONE`) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)* to Save/Load, never as a `FAULTED` transition (release plays on). Save/Load passes the header `state_hash` in EXACT mode, the recorded baseline in REBASED mode when one exists, and otherwise the header value with the verdict `NONE` and the compare skipped; it passes `has_expected_hash = false` only for a WORLD file that legitimately carries no `state_hash` (a release-build file that predates K-4, verdict `NONE`), and no `null`, no `Variant` and no sentinel value is used because a legitimate `H64` of 0 exists (ADR-0002 section 6) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*; F-4 takes `recomputed = computed_hash` and `window_ok = (reported T == header.T)`. The harness compare (dev/test) stays as a second path. Restoring into `PAUSED`, verifying and resuming stays rejected (it conflicts with the Pipeline's `LOADING → RUNNING` `CUT`, with single-player-only pause in CR-16 and with VS-B's reuse of the restore path).)* Integrity here is against accidental corruption, not tampering (host-owned saves, no PvP, no leaderboard).
286:**SL-23 — Determinism, save-scum and wall clock.** Every persisted counter and seed is restored exactly (the kernel's `rng_derive` with counters inside the owners' blocks, G4 and D.10; the Graph keys its random draws by `(step_no, subject_id)` from `world_seed`), so the **physical** world replays the same way (Pillar 1). Whether a **perception** draw (a false system state's onset, sanity drift) replays identically after a restore, or is re-keyed, is Sanity & Hallucination Rules' decision; Save/Load makes no promise either way, and routes the constraint that any re-keying must not be steerable by the player — no reroll oracle through quit or death (OQ-37). *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* **Threat draws and `restore_epoch` (user ruling D16, OQ-47; OQ-49 and OQ-50 closed)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14)*: Attention and Horror re-key their threat draws per restore, while the Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter and seed replay exactly (the first sentence of this paragraph stands, AC-SL-68). Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R1, as amended 2026-10-28 by delegated rulings R13 and R14 (user delegated all remaining calls, including naming the reference machine): **Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`**, a persisted unsigned 32-bit integer that starts at 0 at `new_game` (SL-18) and is stored in the per-slot side-file pair `slot_epoch` (`slot_epoch_a.bin` / `slot_epoch_b.bin`, SL-19), so it survives a process kill, a lost `campaign.json` and a step-back. (0) *Storage (R14)* *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*. The epoch lives in a per-slot **pair** of side files, `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch_a.bin` and `slot_epoch_b.bin` (written `slot_epoch` below), each **12 bytes**: the epoch as a u32 little-endian, a sequence number `seq` as a u32 little-endian, then the CRC32 of those first 8 bytes as a u32 little-endian. The reader takes the valid file (size 12, CRC32 matches) with the higher `seq`; the Save/Load worker always overwrites the **older** file (an invalid file, or the lower `seq`) in place with `seq = max + 1`, flushes, closes, re-reads and checks the CRC32, and that re-read is the `EPOCH_DURABLE` report. There is **no rename, no remove and no `.tmp`**, so there is never an instant with no valid epoch file: a kill mid-write corrupts only the file being written and the other still holds the previous durable value (a single file replaced by rename-over would on Windows probably be remove-then-rename and open an absent-file window, whose rebuild rule could yield a lower epoch than one already advanced and replay a set of threat draws). CRC32 is hand-rolled (polynomial `0xEDB88320`, bitwise, over 8 bytes; `crc32("123456789") == 0xCBF43926` is a unit test) because `PackedByteArray` has no `crc32`. It is in no generation file, so no generation's bytes, trailer SHA-256, `state_hash` or any key derived from them (SL-12's REBASED baseline key included) ever change after `VERIFYING`. Each `WORLD` generation header records the value live when that generation was written (SL-1), a read-only recovery copy that is never rewritten. The value is read once when the campaign is opened (T-6) and held in memory (`e_mem`). (1) *Advance (R13).* A death-stub restore (`DEATH_STUB`) and a `FAULT_RECOVERY` always advance `restore_epoch`. A Continue (`LOAD_GAME`, in-process or after a fresh process start) advances it unless the generation it restores is a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation: that Continue **carries the epoch unchanged** and writes nothing, so a Save & Quit followed by Continue replays the identical threat draws (user ruling D16, "not steerable by quit", outranks R1). A Continue of any other generation (an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation after a kill or crash, or an older generation reached by fallback) advances it. An advance sets `restore_epoch := min(2^32 − 1, max(e_mem, e_slot) + 1)`, `e_slot` the value last read from the `slot_epoch` pair; at 2^32 − 1 it saturates and logs. A step-back, a demotion, a quarantine or a lost manifest cannot lower it. A stub that finds nothing loadable (`SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`) restores nothing and does not advance it. (2) *Durable before the restore is requested (R14).* When an advance is due, Save/Load runs a pre-restore staging step: after selection, pre-check and staging (SL-8, SL-11) it computes the new value and hands the `slot_epoch` write (to the older of the two files) to the worker as its own job, never queued behind a generation write or an abandoned job (SL-10). It polls the job once per frame, never blocking the main thread, and calls `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash, has_expected_hash)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`, so the kernel's `LOADING` holds no wait on Save/Load I/O and stays atomic within one boundary service (kernel CR-15). *Staging interval (`t_epoch_wait`, F-8).* On the death stub the kernel stays `RUNNING` from the `DEAD` boundary to the boundary at which `request_restore` is made: normally one frame, at most `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (30 frames at 60 Hz). During it the seat stays `DEAD`, the hard gate is closed (a seat `DEAD`, a restore pending), and the `restore_pending` latch refuses Save/Load's own capture requests (the dead world is never saved, SL-7) and answers further restore triggers with `SL_LOAD_REENTRANT` *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*. **Save/Load cannot refuse a pause:** pause requests come from PauseGate's own `ControlHandle` (ADR-0002), so if the player pauses during the wait the restore would be requested from `PAUSED`. Either PauseGate or the Chart Table suppresses pause while a seat is `DEAD` (ADR-0030), or `request_restore` is legal from `PAUSED` as well as `RUNNING` (ADR-0003); one of the two is owed by ADR-0003 or ADR-0030 (ADR-0006 OQ-J). The staged payload is immutable, so nothing ticked in the interval reaches the restored world except `PROFILE`-scoped writes (Pillar 5), and the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame. For a Continue the staging runs behind the Continue press, before the kernel is touched; a carried Continue has no staging interval. (2a) *Failure path, a listed exposure.* If the write fails, or `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (placeholder 500, a monotonic I/O timeout) passes without `EPOCH_DURABLE`, Save/Load still calls `request_restore` with the advanced value held in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED`, because the device is failing and saving is impossible anyway. The worker re-attempts the `slot_epoch` write with the next write job, and after every later `WRITTEN` generation Save/Load rewrites the `slot_epoch` pair whenever the in-memory value is ahead of the file. A kill before a later successful write may replay that epoch once (OQ-25). (2b) *Recovery copy* *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*. When **both** `slot_epoch` files are missing or invalid (one valid file is a normal read, not a failure), the value reads as `max(the newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT` and is rewritten by the worker into the older slot; because the pair removes the remove-then-rename window, a missing pair is reachable only by tampering, a first-ever write interrupted at creation, or media loss. Deleting the side files by hand therefore re-keys the next stretch once, a tampering exposure of the same class as editing any save file (OQ-25). (3) *Reach into the sim.* `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash, has_expected_hash)` hands the value to the kernel, which exposes it read-only, sim-visible and pure in `kernel.clock` as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` before the first `restore()`. The kernel owns the one derivation for threat draws, `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` (`RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` 1 048 576, owned by the kernel; the stream-name hash stays cached and unchanged); Attention and Horror call that derivation and define none of their own, and the name `threat_epoch()` is retired in favour of `restore_epoch`. The Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter never read it. (4) *Determinism is defined given the pair:* the same (save bytes, `restore_epoch`) replays identically, and tests pin the epoch (AC-SL-142, AC-SL-145). (5) *What it prices, stated plainly:* the player can neither pick nor predict the new value; a death re-keys the next stretch (the price, metric M2); a Save & Quit followed by Continue carries the epoch (R13), so the threat draws after it are those an uninterrupted run would meet and quit buys nothing (metric M3 measures only the disguised manual save); a kill then Continue of an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation advances it, priced by the minutes lost since that autosave (OQ-25). A kill after a carried Continue, followed by a second Continue of the same `QUIT` generation, also carries the epoch and replays that stretch exactly, a repeat and not a re-key, an accepted exposure of the same kind as OQ-25's kill. The cleaner fix is to refresh the stored hash at the first mutator that touches the instance — LM2's attach step already mutates the row, so it can write current template hashes there instead of during restore. That keeps restore as a true identity operation, preserves EXACT, and still lets the history-based check work correctly since by weld time the hash matches the current template; any drift before weld is harmlessly re-diagnosed each load.
