My fix is to never rewrite during restore — keep stored hashes byte-identical, raise diagnostics on each load, and refresh an instance's stored hashes against the current template at the moment it acquires history (LM2, LM3, LM4), so the history rule always compares against the template the history was actually made under. I'm also considering an alternative where ADR-0006 gains a new CONTENT_DRIFT_ACCEPTED cause reported via context, and noting that ADR-0016 §9.3 needs a corresponding update, while the structure-hash refusal path stays unchanged.

A second high-severity blocking issue: RAGGED-cut stub HULL_SEGMENT nodes get appended outside their section's contiguous node range, which breaks the pure comparison count check and the bsearch-based reverse lookup from Graph id to section, and also causes problems with discarded/tombstoned sections. My fix is to redefine the range check to allow tombstones for discarded instances, and to have section_counts_into report template-range counts plus a separate stub_count, adjusting or skipping logic appropriately for discarded sections.

I also realize reverse lookup should only apply to template-range ids — stub nodes need to resolve through GraphView.section_of and the seam's stub list, with anchor geometry coming from the cut socket's hatch rect via Layout. This is HIGH severity and blocking.

Moving to T3 MEDIUM blocking: there's a setup/port ordering cycle and ambiguity around RoomSource — Architecture.md registers Layout before Graph, but Layout.setup needs a port that Graph's facade provides later, and Graph.setup needs a RoomSource that ADR-0013 never actually names. My amendment is to have LayoutViews constructed during LayoutModule.setup itself, implementing ADR-0011's RoomSource interface and exposed via layout.room_source() for the composition root, while LayoutGraphPort gets bound through a late bind_graph call before freeze or via a composition-root-level adapter.

For T4 MEDIUM non-blocking, I'm cataloging naming drift between LayoutGraphPort and the actual Graph-side names (check_instantiate vs check_instantiate_section, SectionBases vs InstantiateResult), plus seam_view bypassing the port in places, and opening_into validity scoping needing to include INIT phase since LM1 seeding happens in init_world — along with mapping Graph's ONSET_UNKEYED reason into Layout's closed can_build set.

Then for T5 MEDIUM non-blocking, I'm tracking missing cross-references owed to sibling ADRs — body_is_live and section_contains from ADR-0015, node_base and template emitter placements from ADR-0017, RectFlags bit values and SlotFeed from ADR-0014 — plus noting that section_rects_into is section-keyed but returns body-frame data, which conflicts with the "no frame mixing" rule in §11, so I need to add an amendment addressing that.

Now I'm compiling a running table of these amendments: T6 flags that §13's kind_ordinal is missing JAMB even though §5 reserves JAMB slots and ADR-0034 needs it; T7 notes a version-tracking mismatch between ADR-0014's invalidate and §10's changed_region behavior after restore; T8 catches a contradictory sentence in post_restore about whether a fault is clamped-with-diagnostic or triggers LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING, resolving it in favor of the fault per TR-section-035; T9 identifies that weld canonicalisation only holds for layout.state since graph.state's seam row order can differ between attach(x,y) and attach(y,x), so I'm proposing socket_plan canonicalise via survivor_of and asserting whole-world state_hash equality instead; and T10 is flagging that the S1 row in architecture.md for spike gating omits a reference to ADR-0013.

Then I move into cross_adr ownership assignments — C1 covers the ADR-0006/0016 rebase issue owned by ADR-0013, C2 assigns the missing LayoutGraphPort implementer to ADR-0011, C3 assigns the RoomSource/setup cycle to ADR-0013 despite ADR-0011 involvement, and C4 starts assigning stub-node and section_counts_into semantics ownership to ADR-0011 across multiple related ADRs.

C5 settles section_rects_into frame ambiguity by assigning ADR-0034 to fix its section-local assumption against ADR-0014's body frame, spanning ADRs 0013/0014/0034. C6 and C7 assign JAMB and discard-invalidate/version_epoch ownership to ADR-0013, with C7 also noting adoption of ADR-0014, and I'm now starting on C8 regarding the can_* naming divergence.

input.verdict: CONCERNS. The core decisions are sound and right-sized for a solo MVP. They are: instances by reference with dense SoA columns, dense ids with id == row + 1, the Layout/Graph id split, the lower-body_id weld survivor, a reserved idx space, and the third structure_hash, which has a concrete failing scenario behind it. The engine version is stamped (4.7.2, MEDIUM risk), and both 4.7 rows that apply (packed-array element writes and the typed-return override) are flagged. V1 is probed and V2 to V5 are named as UNVERIFIED. The alternatives were genuinely considered, and the Consequences section is honest about touch_serial churn, the LEAF family and the harsh refusal of reordered templates. Marking the LEAF key from the HOOK scope is legal under ADR-0003 (open_for in HOOK) and ADR-0004 section 7 (a mark is not a diff). TR traceability is complete: all 35 rows tagged ADR-0013 are addressed (20 decided, 12 shared, 3 owned elsewhere). Three items block Accept: (T1) the drift-policy hash rewrite inside restore() contradicts ADR-0006 SL-12's closed set of REBASED causes; (T2) the contiguous-range verification and reverse lookup ignore the HULL_SEGMENT stub rows that a RAGGED cut appends; (T3) the setup/port injection cycle with the Graph is unresolved, and the RoomSource port that ADR-0011 depends on is not declared.

findings.text: Section 10's drift policy rewrites an instance's stored geometry_hash or visual_hash inside restore() when it accepts geometry_changed_fresh or visual_changed. The section then says the resulting K-4 state_hash mismatch is reported 'as a diagnostic, as designed'. That is false under ADR-0006 and the Save/Load GDD SL-12. A rewritten hash makes snapshot(restore(x)) != x. The five REBASED causes are a closed set (migration, retired strip, default fill, hash_algo, a REBASE_BLOCKS member), and none of them covers an owner-side content-drift rewrite. ADR-0016 section 9.3 says the case is 'accepted as a REBASED case' but names no cause. In EXACT mode the result is NOT_REPRODUCED, which halts dev and test builds and marks the generation suspect in release. A visual-only art tweak to a section template, the most common edit before release, would therefore halt every dev load of every existing save.
findings.amendment: Make restore() byte-identical. Never rewrite a stored hash in restore(): keep the stored values in LayoutState, raise geometry_changed_fresh or visual_changed (re-raised on each load until the instance changes), and re-derive the rects from the current template, which already happens because rects are derived. Refresh an instance's three stored hashes from the current template inside LM2 attach_section, the moment the instance first gets history. The history-dependent geometry rule then compares against the template that history was made under, and a later weld cannot cause a false refusal. Strike the sentence ending 'as designed'. Add a Validation criterion: after a visual-only and after a fresh-geometry template edit, the load verifies EXACT/MATCH. If this is rejected, the alternative is an ADR-0006 amendment that adds a sixth REBASED cause (content drift accepted) reported through ctx. That option costs more.

findings.text: Section 3 and section 10 (d) assume each section's Graph ids are exactly the contiguous ranges [node_base, node_base + template count). The post-restore check 'node, edge and compartment counts match the template' is described as a pure comparison, and the reverse lookup from Graph id to section is a bsearch over node_base. ADR-0011 sections 3.6 and 4.1 (3) say a RAGGED cut_detach appends the hull stubs as ordinary HULL_SEGMENT node rows, flagged STUB, with fresh high ids, and discard_section tombstones every row of a section. If section_counts_into counts by section_id, every save made after a RAGGED cut fails Layout's post_restore and takes LOADING to FAULTED. If it does not, the bsearch reverse lookup still answers NONE for a stub id. anchor_geometry and plate_positions then return nothing for a leaking stub that Failure & Trail and the Emitter's fault glow need to place.
findings.amendment: Define check (d) precisely. For each non-discarded instance, the rows in [node_base, node_base + template.node_count) and the matching edge range resolve to section s and are not tombstoned, and compartment k == comp_base + k. Rows outside the template range (STUB rows, seam edges) are excluded. For a discarded instance, the same ranges resolve to tombstones of section s. State in section 3 that the bsearch mapping covers template-range ids only. Stub nodes resolve through GraphView.section_of(id) plus the seam's stub list, and anchor_geometry for a stub answers the cut socket's hatch span, or explicitly NONE with a named owner for its placement. Add a fixture: RAGGED cut, save, restore, verify passes and anchor_geometry(stub) is as specified.

findings.text: The construction order is circular and incompletely declared. architecture.md section 8 sets up Layout before the Graph. LayoutModule.setup(facet, templates, tuning, graph: LayoutGraphPort) needs the Graph facade, but GraphModule.setup(facet, tuning, catalog, rooms: RoomSource, strict_numeric) runs later and needs a RoomSource that ADR-0011 says 'Layout's read view implements'. ADR-0013 never mentions RoomSource (room_volume_tiles and room_exposed_tiles, -1 for an unknown room). Its read_view facade is put at registry freeze, which is after both setups. A Layout story cannot be written against this.
findings.amendment: In section 1 and Key Interfaces, state that LayoutViews is constructed inside LayoutModule.setup and lives for the whole process, and that it implements ADR-0011's @abstract RoomSource (exposed as layout.room_source() for the composition root). List room_volume_tiles and room_exposed_tiles in section 11 Tier H with their sentinels. Break the cycle explicitly, for example with a LayoutModule.bind_graph(port: LayoutGraphPort) that the composition root calls after GraphModule.setup and before the registry freeze. Port calls before the freeze are a defect (asserted). Then update the architecture.md section 8 step 4 note.

findings.text: LayoutGraphPort has drifted from the Graph side. The port says check_instantiate and SectionBases; ADR-0011 and ADR-0012 say check_instantiate_section and InstantiateResult. Section 3's table lists a 'comp counter in graph.state', but ADR-0011 has four counters and comp_base == node_base because compartments are COMPARTMENT nodes. Section 3 and section 7 (LM2) read seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids, which bypasses the port that section 8 calls Layout's only route to the Graph. Section 8 says opening_into is valid 'in P3 and in P2', but LM1 seeds leaves in the INIT scope of init_world. can_build's closed reason set maps any Graph refusal to CAPACITY, yet check_instantiate_section can return ONSET_UNKEYED and the other LS-18 reasons.
findings.amendment: Rename the port members to ADR-0011's names (InstantiateResult, check_instantiate_section). Change the section 3 compartment row to 'COMPARTMENT node ids; comp_base == node_base (ADR-0011 section 4.4)'. Replace both seam_view references with seam_openings_into. Add INIT to the scopes where the port reads are valid. State that can_build passes a Graph reason through as layout.GRAPH_<REASON>, or that the reason is unreachable at runtime because the ADR-0007 template validator calls graph_rules.onset_valid at boot.

findings.text: Section 11 does not list reads that Core siblings have already built on. ADR-0015 needs body_is_live(body_id) and section_contains(section_id, x, y). ADR-0017 E1 needs node_base(section_id) and an emitter-placement accessor on SectionTemplate (def_id, anchor, node_ordinal, switch_on, subkind); section 4 names only fixture_anchors and instrument_placements. ADR-0014 needs the RectFlags bit values and file and the SlotFeed (slot_count, slot_footprint, slot_extent), and it adds section_rects_into, which is keyed by section but answers in the body frame. That breaks this ADR's frame rule in section 5 and section 11 ('Every geometry read answers section-local'; 'A read never mixes frames') unless the rule is amended.
findings.amendment: Add a 'Reads owed to Core siblings' table to section 11 with exact signatures and tiers: body_is_live, section_contains, node_base/edge_base/comp_base getters, SectionTemplate.emitter_placement_* idx accessors, src/sim/layout/rect_flags.gd with its bit values and ALL mask, and the SlotFeed. Add section_rects_into to the section 5 list of body-frame reads as the one section-keyed exception.

findings.text: Section 13 closes the kind_ordinal vocabulary at six kinds (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar), but section 5 reserves a JAMB variant slot for every hatched socket, TR-assembly-045 names jambs, and ADR-0034 assigns JAMB 7 (its OQ-C).
findings.amendment: Add JAMB to the section 13 closed vocabulary. Ordinal values stay ADR-0034's.

findings.text: The version-counter text predates ADR-0014. Section 10 says the restore resets counters to 1 and that 'every rebuilding consumer rebuilds on tick 1', and that every section reports changed_region ALL once after a restore. ADR-0014 (section 6) shows the ALL stamp is not guaranteed to be seen. It makes version_epoch the authoritative restore signal and replaces LM4's bump with invalidate (all three counters set to 0). Section 9's LM4 row states no version effect at all.
findings.amendment: In section 9 (LM4) and section 10, adopt ADR-0014's invalidate on discard and new_epoch() on restore/default_state. Cite version_epoch as the consumer rebuild signal, and demote 'changed_region ALL after restore' to a non-guaranteed hint.

findings.text: Section 10 post_restore (a) contradicts itself: 'an area above area_max is clamped with a diagnostic, and the same fault found here is LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING'. One case cannot be both a clamp-and-continue and a fault that takes LOADING to FAULTED.
findings.amendment: Follow TR-section-035: in post_restore an area above area_max is LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING via ctx.fault (no clamp). In the layout.doors hook it is clamped with area_clamped.

findings.text: Weld canonicalisation stops at layout.state. socket_plan(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b) fills the Graph's JoinPlan in argument order, so graph.state's seam row (section_a/section_b, opening order) can differ between attach(x, y) and attach(y, x). The Consequence 'same bytes for the same world regardless of argument order, so state_hash equality and replay hold' is proved only for layout.state.
findings.amendment: Have socket_plan canonicalise to survivor-first through weld_math.survivor_of, so JoinPlan and opening_ids are argument-order independent. Extend the weld-symmetry Validation criterion to whole-world state_hash equality.

findings.text: Spike gating is honest in the text (V2 and V3 are pending S1 figures with ADR-0010's fallback ladder; V4 waits on ADR-0005). However, architecture.md's S1 / SP-ENG-1 row lists ADR-0012, 0014, 0015 and 0017 but not ADR-0013, and the ADR never states whether Accept is gated on S1. OQ-2 (line 1367 of requirements-traceability.md still reads ADR-0013 + ADR-0007 for TR-derelict-034) is still open.
findings.amendment: State in Engine Compatibility that Accept is not gated on V2/V3 (they are cost lines with a fallback, and no data shape depends on them), while V4 golden vectors gate the template-hash story. Route to /architecture-review: add ADR-0013 V2/V3 to the S1 row and fix summary line 1367.

cross_adr.text: The drift-policy hash rewrite in Layout restore() has no REBASED cause in ADR-0006's closed set of five. ADR-0016 section 9.3 says it is 'accepted as a REBASED case' without naming one.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0013 removes the rewrite from restore() and refreshes the hashes in LM2 (T1). ADR-0016 section 9.3 then replaces its sentence with 'layout.state restore is byte-identical; content drift is diagnostic only'. ADR-0006 needs no change.

cross_adr.text: No implementer of LayoutGraphPort exists. ADR-0011 publishes no opening_into, seam_openings_into, section_counts_into or check_instantiate/LayoutGraphPort facade. It has GraphView.opening_area, seam_view and InstantiateResult instead.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 adds to its Key Interfaces a Graph-side adapter that extends LayoutGraphPort (allocation-free opening_into, seam_openings_into in socket_plan.openings order, section_counts_into, check_instantiate_section, instantiate_section with InstantiateResult), valid in the APPLY, INIT, HOOK and post_restore phases.

cross_adr.text: RAGGED-cut stub HULL_SEGMENT rows and discard tombstones fall outside or within a section's contiguous M1 range in ways that section_counts_into does not define. Layout's post-restore check (d), ADR-0016's verifier V2 and the reverse id-to-section lookup depend on that definition.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 defines section_counts_into's out as template-range counts (nodes, edges, compartments created by M1) plus a separate stub_count, with tombstone status reported, and states that a stub's section_of is the cut section. ADR-0013 (T2) adjusts its check and its reverse lookup to match.

cross_adr.text: Setup cycle: Layout is set up first and needs LayoutGraphPort, while the Graph's setup needs Layout's RoomSource. ADR-0013 does not declare RoomSource.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0013 constructs LayoutViews in setup, implements RoomSource, exposes room_source(), and adds bind_graph(port) called after GraphModule.setup and before the freeze (T3). architecture.md section 8 notes the binding step.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0034's assumption says section_rects_into rows carry the extent 'in section-local px', but ADR-0014 section 5 defines section_rects_into as answering in the body frame, with occupied spans (x1 - 1, y1 - 1).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0034 restates its assumption to body-frame occupied spans and converts by subtracting section_offset when it builds section-parented sprites. ADR-0013 lists the exception in its frame rule (T5).

cross_adr.text: JAMB is missing from ADR-0013's closed kind_ordinal vocabulary. ADR-0034 assigns JAMB 7 (OQ-C).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0013 section 13 adds JAMB (T6). ADR-0034 then closes OQ-C.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0014 replaces LM4's version bump with invalidate (counters set to 0) and adds version_epoch as the restore signal. ADR-0013's sections 9 and 10 do not reflect either.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0013 adopts invalidate on discard and new_epoch() on restore/default_state, and cites version_epoch (T7).

cross_adr.text: Reads that siblings consume are not published in ADR-0013 section 11: body_is_live and section_contains (ADR-0015), node_base(section_id) and template emitter placements (ADR-0017), the RectFlags file and the SlotFeed (ADR-0014).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0013 section 11 adds a 'Reads owed to Core siblings' table with signatures and tiers (T5).

cross_adr.text: The Class A pure check is named check_* in ADR-0003 section 5 and the registry, while Layout keeps the GDD-published can_* names with the identical shape.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0003 amends section 5 to 'a pure check, conventionally check_*; an owner may keep a GDD-published can_* name with the same shape', so the registry stance mutator_status admits both.

cross_adr.text: Weld argument-order independence is guaranteed for layout.state only. JoinPlan is filled in caller argument order, so graph.state seam rows can differ between attach(x, y) and attach(y, x).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0013's socket_plan canonicalises survivor-first (T9). ADR-0021's weld property test asserts whole-world state_hash equality for reversed arguments.

data.verdict: CONCERNS. The core decisions are sound and right-sized for a solo MVP. They are: instances by reference with dense SoA columns, dense ids with id == row + 1, the Layout/Graph id split, the lower-body_id weld survivor, a reserved idx space, and the third structure_hash, which has a concrete failing scenario behind it. The engine version is stamped (4.7.2, MEDIUM risk), and both 4.7 rows that apply (packed-array element writes and the typed-return override) are flagged. V1 is probed and V2 to V5 are named as UNVERIFIED. The alternatives were genuinely considered, and the Consequences section is honest about touch_serial churn, the LEAF family and the harsh refusal of reordered templates. Marking the LEAF key from the HOOK scope is legal under ADR-0003 (open_for in HOOK) and ADR-0004 section 7 (a mark is not a diff). TR traceability is complete: all 35 rows tagged ADR-0013 are addressed (20 decided, 12 shared, 3 owned elsewhere). Three items block Accept: (T1) the drift-policy hash rewrite inside restore() contradicts ADR-0006 SL-12's closed set of REBASED causes; (T2) the contiguous-range verification and reverse lookup ignore the HULL_SEGMENT stub rows that a RAGGED cut appends; (T3) the setup/port injection cycle with the Graph is unresolved, and the RoomSource port that ADR-0011 depends on is not declared.

findings.text: Section 10's drift policy rewrites an instance's stored geometry_hash or visual_hash inside restore() when it accepts geometry_changed_fresh or visual_changed. The section then says the resulting K-4 state_hash mismatch is reported 'as a diagnostic, as designed'. That is false under ADR-0006 and the Save/Load GDD SL-12. A rewritten hash makes snapshot(restore(x)) != x. The five REBASED causes are a closed set (migration, retired strip, default fill, hash_algo, a REBASE_BLOCKS member), and none of them covers an owner-side content-drift rewrite. ADR-0016 section 9.3 says the case is 'accepted as a REBASED case' but names no cause. In EXACT mode the result is NOT_REPRODUCED, which halts dev and test builds and marks the generation suspect in release. A visual-only art tweak to a section template, the most common edit before release, would therefore halt every dev load of every existing save.
findings.amendment: Make restore() byte-identical. Never rewrite a stored hash in restore(): keep the stored values in LayoutState, raise geometry_changed_fresh or visual_changed (re-raised on each load until the instance changes), and re-derive the rects from the current template, which already happens because rects are derived. Refresh an instance's three stored hashes from the current template inside LM2 attach_section, the moment the instance first gets history. The history-dependent geometry rule then compares against the template that history was made under, and a later weld cannot cause a false refusal. Strike the sentence ending 'as designed'. Add a Validation criterion: after a visual-only and after a fresh-geometry template edit, the load verifies EXACT/MATCH. If this is rejected, the alternative is an ADR-0006 amendment that adds a sixth REBASED cause (content drift accepted) reported through ctx. That option costs more.

findings.text: Section 3 and section 10 (d) assume each section's Graph ids are exactly the contiguous ranges [node_base, node_base + template count). The post-restore check 'node, edge and compartment counts match the template' is described as a pure comparison, and the reverse lookup from Graph id to section is a bsearch over node_base. ADR-0011 sections 3.6 and 4.1 (3) say a RAGGED cut_detach appends the hull stubs as ordinary HULL_SEGMENT node rows, flagged STUB, with fresh high ids, and discard_section tombstones every row of a section. If section_counts_into counts by section_id, every save made after a RAGGED cut fails Layout's post_restore and takes LOADING to FAULTED. If it does not, the bsearch reverse lookup still answers NONE for a stub id. anchor_geometry and plate_positions then return nothing for a leaking stub that Failure & Trail and the Emitter's fault glow need to place.
findings.amendment: Define check (d) precisely. For each non-discarded instance, the rows in [node_base, node_base + template.node_count) and the matching edge range resolve to section s and are not tombstoned, and compartment k == comp_base + k. Rows outside the template range (STUB rows, seam edges) are excluded. For a discarded instance, the same ranges resolve to tombstones of section s. State in section 3 that the bsearch mapping covers template-range ids only. Stub nodes resolve through GraphView.section_of(id) plus the seam's stub list, and anchor_geometry for a stub answers the cut socket's hatch span, or explicitly NONE with a named owner for its placement. Add a fixture: RAGGED cut, save, restore, verify passes and anchor_geometry(stub) is as specified.

findings.text: The construction order is circular and incompletely declared. architecture.md section 8 sets up Layout before the Graph. LayoutModule.setup(facet, templates, tuning, graph: LayoutGraphPort) needs the Graph facade, but GraphModule.setup(facet, tuning, catalog, rooms: RoomSource, strict_numeric) runs later and needs a RoomSource that ADR-0011 says 'Layout's read view implements'. ADR-0013 never mentions RoomSource (room_volume_tiles and room_exposed_tiles, -1 for an unknown room). Its read_view facade is put at registry freeze, which is after both setups. A Layout story cannot be written against this.
findings.amendment: In section 1 and Key Interfaces, state that LayoutViews is constructed inside LayoutModule.setup and lives for the whole process, and that it implements ADR-0011's @abstract RoomSource (exposed as layout.room_source() for the composition root). List room_volume_tiles and room_exposed_tiles in section 11 Tier H with their sentinels. Break the cycle explicitly, for example with a LayoutModule.bind_graph(port: LayoutGraphPort) that the composition root calls after GraphModule.setup and before the registry freeze. Port calls before the freeze are a defect (asserted). Then update the architecture.md section 8 step 4 note.

findings.text: LayoutGraphPort has drifted from the Graph side. The port says check_instantiate and SectionBases; ADR-0011 and ADR-0012 say check_instantiate_section and InstantiateResult. Section 3's table lists a 'comp counter in graph.state', but ADR-0011 has four counters and comp_base == node_base because compartments are COMPARTMENT nodes. Section 3 and section 7 (LM2) read seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids, which bypasses the port that section 8 calls Layout's only route to the Graph. Section 8 says opening_into is valid 'in P3 and in P2', but LM1 seeds leaves in the INIT scope of init_world. can_build's closed reason set maps any Graph refusal to CAPACITY, yet check_instantiate_section can return ONSET_UNKEYED and the other LS-18 reasons.
findings.amendment: Rename the port members to ADR-0011's names (InstantiateResult, check_instantiate_section). Change the section 3 compartment row to 'COMPARTMENT node ids; comp_base == node_base (ADR-0011 section 4.4)'. Replace both seam_view references with seam_openings_into. Add INIT to the scopes where the port reads are valid. State that can_build passes a Graph reason through as layout.GRAPH_<REASON>, or that the reason is unreachable at runtime because the ADR-0007 template validator calls graph_rules.onset_valid at boot.

findings.text: Section 11 does not list reads that Core siblings have already built on. ADR-0015 needs body_is_live(body_id) and section_contains(section_id, x, y). ADR-0017 E1 needs node_base(section_id) and an emitter-placement accessor on SectionTemplate (def_id, anchor, node_ordinal, switch_on, subkind); section 4 names only fixture_anchors and instrument_placements. ADR-0014 needs the RectFlags bit values and file and the SlotFeed (slot_count, slot_footprint, slot_extent), and it adds section_rects_into, which is keyed by section but answers in the body frame. That breaks this ADR's frame rule in section 5 and section 11 ('Every geometry read answers section-local'; 'A read never mixes frames') unless the rule is amended.
findings.amendment: Add a 'Reads owed to Core siblings' table to section 11 with exact signatures and tiers: body_is_live, section_contains, node_base/edge_base/comp_base getters, SectionTemplate.emitter_placement_* idx accessors, src/sim/layout/rect_flags.gd with its bit values and ALL mask, and the SlotFeed. Add section_rects_into to the section 5 list of body-frame reads as the one section-keyed exception.

findings.text: Section 13 closes the kind_ordinal vocabulary at six kinds (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar), but section 5 reserves a JAMB variant slot for every hatched socket, TR-assembly-045 names jambs, and ADR-0034 assigns JAMB 7 (its OQ-C).
findings.amendment: Add JAMB to the section 13 closed vocabulary. Ordinal values stay ADR-0034's.

findings.text: The version-counter text predates ADR-0014. Section 10 says the restore resets counters to 1 and that 'every rebuilding consumer rebuilds on tick 1', and that every section reports changed_region ALL once after a restore. ADR-0014 (section 6) shows the ALL stamp is not guaranteed to be seen. It makes version_epoch the authoritative restore signal and replaces LM4's bump with invalidate (all three counters set to 0). Section 9's LM4 row states no version effect at all.
findings.amendment: In section 9 (LM4) and section 10, adopt ADR-0014's invalidate on discard and new_epoch() on restore/default_state. Cite version_epoch as the consumer rebuild signal, and demote 'changed_region ALL after restore' to a non-guaranteed hint.

findings.text: Section 10 post_restore (a) contradicts itself: 'an area above area_max is clamped with a diagnostic, and the same fault found here is LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING'. One case cannot be both a clamp-and-continue and a fault that takes LOADING to FAULTED.
findings.amendment: Follow TR-section-035: in post_restore an area above area_max is LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING via ctx.fault (no clamp). In the layout.doors hook it is clamped with area_clamped.
